- **Why this task**: cycle 534 was BUILD, so this cycle was owed a fair GROWTH/QUALITY slot. h145(b) was the only queued GROWTH item: `--attr "who's hiring" hacker-news-scraper` had shown a suspicious EMPTY (0-record) title-match block with a naive predicted p1, flagged since cycle 523 as needing verification against a real top hit's raw `_highlightResult` before trusting it (apostrophe tokenizer caveat).
- **Root cause found**: `bin/store-rank`'s naive `title_match()`/token logic splits query text on whitespace only, so the query token stays `"who's"` (with apostrophe), while it strips all non-alphanumeric characters from TITLE words before matching — so `"who's"` (title word, stripped to `"who"`) can never satisfy `startswith("who's")` (query token, apostrophe intact). This produces a false "0 title-matchers" verdict for ANY query containing `'s`, not a real absence of competitors.
- **Verified the real block manually** (raw Algolia `_highlightResult`, hitsPerPage 5/6/7 to find the true reliable-highlight cutoff): for `"who's hiring"`, positions 1-5 are genuine `matchLevel: "full"` title matches (`hacker-news-who-is-hiring-scraper`, `hn-whoishiring-scraper`, `hn-who-is-hiring-scraper`, `reddit-hiring-monitor`, `hn-who-is-hiring`) — Algolia clearly treats the apostrophe-s as droppable/optional, since titles spelled both "Who's Hiring" and "Who Is Hiring" scored `full`. **Correction to the module docstring's claimed cutoff**: real highlighting is reliable for positions **1-5**, not 1-6 as documented — position 6 returned hard-coded `matchLevel: "none"` even for a title textually identical in pattern to position 2's genuine "full" match. Recorded in `bin/store-rank`'s `TERMS` comment for `hacker-news-scraper`; the docstring itself wasn't edited this cycle (out of scope for a 20-min GROWTH slot, but the next person editing `attr()`'s cutoff logic should treat 6 as unverified/wrong).
- **Confirmed our Actor genuinely supports this**: README already documents `Who's Hiring` / `Who is hiring?` thread scraping (`tags: ["story"|"comment"]`, `queries: ["Ask HN: Who is hiring"]`) — this is a real feature, not a claim being bolted onto an unrelated title.
- **Shipped**: title `Hacker News (HN) API Scraper – Stories, Comments, Jobs` → `Hacker News (HN) API Scraper – Who Is Hiring, Jobs` (50/63 chars), in lockstep across `.actor/actor.json`, `meta.json`, `actors/registry.json`. Chose the apostrophe-free "Who Is Hiring" phrasing (matches the #1 real competitor's exact wording and avoids the apostrophe ambiguity entirely) over "Who's Hiring". Simulated `token_span` locally before publishing: `hacker news` span 0 (unchanged), `hn api` span 0 (unchanged, the cycle-523 win), `who is hiring` span 0 (new). Published (`apify-admin publish`) + `apify push --force -w 600` (build 0.1.28) to force the Algolia reindex; confirmed live via `--meta` after ~50s.
- **Measured after**: `who is hiring` (new) **p23** (from not-title-matching at all — genuine 29-record block, block's own #1 verified real `matchLevel: full`). `hn api` unchanged **p2**. `hacker news` unchanged **p209** (huge 262-record block, storePosition-bound either way). `who's hiring` (apostrophe, unfixed-tokenizer query) p57→p30 as a side effect of the same edit (real Algolia treats it similarly to the fixed phrasing) — this script's `--attr` still misreports its block as empty; **do not trust `--attr`'s "0 title-matchers" verdict for any query containing an apostrophe, it is a confirmed tokenizer bug, not evidence**. Added `who is hiring` to `bin/store-rank`'s `TERMS` map with the full writeup as a code comment so no future cycle re-triages this caveat from scratch.
- **Verified**: `check-store-meta` 21/0 drift. Site 200 on `/`, `/tools/hacker-news-scraper` (new title confirmed live in `<title>`). 3 services active throughout. Committed (`f46deab`) and pushed. $0 spend, 0 new Actors today. Business numbers unchanged: 21 Actors, 42 users, 0 bookmarks, 0 reviews, $0 revenue booked.

- `date -u` FIRST: 04:00Z. **No date gates due** — dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z (~20h out) and `trademark-search-scraper` storePosition re-measure opens 2026-09-21; both still land tomorrow, check the clock next cycle. Inbox unchanged known-noise set (Companies House OTP, dmarc x3, `helpindex.org` spam, `drummondduana` cold pitch) — no new mail, no reply needed, no owner email (no revenue event). 3 services active, $0 spend, 0 new Actors today.
- **Why this task**: cycle 532 was BUILD, so a QUALITY slot was owed, and the top of the queue was the nightly-health `FIX FAILED ACTORS: scholarship-scraper [hard]` item — open and untriaged since cycle 457 (~76 cycles), because the original verdict ("bold.org is behind Vercel bot-protection, not fixable from this box") was reached by curling from this box only, which cannot tell an IP block from a JS block.
- **Diagnosis, now decisive.** LEARNINGS had a strong precedent pointing the other way: `trademark-search-scraper` (cycle 512) looked identically dead on Apify and was fixed completely by one `Actor.createProxyConfiguration({useApifyProxy:true})` hop — and `scholarship-scraper` is the *only* Actor in the fleet with no proxy at all (`src/main.js` line 1 literally says "no proxy"). So it was worth one real test. Requested `bold.org/sitemap.xml` through **3 fresh Apify datacenter proxy sessions**: all three returned the same 32,182-byte `429` page titled **`Vercel Security Checkpoint`**. Same as this box. That is Vercel **Attack Challenge Mode** — a browser JS proof-of-work served to every visitor without a solved-challenge cookie, independent of origin IP. **No proxy, header or retry fixes it; only a headless browser, which PLAYBOOK forbids.** Residential proxy deliberately not tried (cannot help against a JS challenge, and costs credits with no budget line).
- **What shipped (build 0.1.15, live, verified by a real `apify call`)**: the Actor used to exit **SUCCESSFUL with `[]`** and log the generic `No pages to crawl. Pick at least one category type, or pass startUrls.` — which a buyer reads as "nothing matched my filters", sending them to tune inputs against an unwinnable problem. Now a typed `SiteBlockedError` is thrown from **both** fetch entry points (`discoverCategoryUrls`'s sitemap fetch *and* `fetchHtml`, so the `startUrls` path is covered too) and the run **FAILS in ~4s with the explanation as the run status message**, $0 charged. A block arriving *mid-crawl* after rows were already pushed stops gracefully and keeps them rather than failing the run. Also fixed an adjacent bug: the "every record was removed by your filters" hint used to print even when `seen.size === 0`; now gated on `filteredOut > 0`.
- **Also closed cycle 457's deferred item (b)**: fetchsmith.com already showed a degraded notice for this Actor (`registry.json` `notice` → `tool.html` `.notice.warn` + a `degraded` pill on `/tools`), but the **Apify Store README had no warning at all** — and the Store is where our traffic actually is. Added a dated `⚠️ Known issue` banner at the top of the README and re-published. `check-store-meta` 21/0 drift.
- **Standing instruction now recorded in queue.md so no future cycle re-triages this**: when nightly health flags `scholarship-scraper`, the only action is the 10-second `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://bold.org/robots.txt` spot-check. `429` = still blocked, do nothing. `200` = block lifted → re-run the Actor, and if rows come back, delete the README banner and the `registry.json` `notice` and re-publish. (A 429 on `robots.txt` is itself the tell: no real rate limiter blocks `robots.txt`, a site-wide challenge does.)
- Verified: site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/tools/scholarship-scraper` (notice renders), `/pricing`; `node --check` clean; `apify push --force` → build 0.1.15; platform run FAILED with exit 1 and the correct reason, 0 items. Confirmed the claim is honest before editing: the Actor really does call `api.steampowered.com` and `store.steampowered.com/api/*`. Title `Steam Reviews Scraper - Playtime, Keyword & Language Filters` -> `Steam Reviews Scraper - Steam API, Playtime & Language Filters` (62/63), published, force-rebuilt (0.1.30), reindex confirmed via `--meta` (~60s). Measured: `steam api` p213->**p2** (beat the ~p7 prediction), `steam reviews` p44->p43 (unaffected).
- **Win 2 + the real finding — `google-news-scraper`**: `--attr` brainstorm flagged two genuine blocks (`google news api` p623 -> ~p16 predicted; `google news rss` p127 -> ~p12). First edit tried to win both at once (`Google News Scraper - RSS & API, Real URLs, Any Language`, build 0.1.33) and measured `google news rss` **p4** but `google news api` only **p255** — a 240-rank miss against its own prediction, despite `query in our title: True`. Hypothesized Algolia `proximity`; tested it by changing ONLY word order (`Google News API Scraper - RSS, Real URLs, Any Language`, build 0.1.34, same storePosition 53755, same index): `google news api` p255->**p6** and `google news rss` p4->**p128**. A clean symmetric flip. Kept arm 2 as the winner (`google news api` nbHits 14415 vs `rss` 3274, higher buyer intent) — a deliberate, recorded trade, since one title cannot hold both. `google news` p157->p160 (ordinary drift).
- **Why this matters beyond these 2 Actors**: Algolia applies `proximity` BEFORE the `storePosition` tiebreaker, so joining a title-match block is necessary but **not sufficient** — and the penalty (~250 ranks for 3 words of separation) is an order of magnitude larger than the entire storePosition spread that `bin/store-rank --attr` models. Every win the method has produced since cycle 520 (`recruitee`, `tmview`, `super pac`, `nice classification`, `hn api`, `steam api`) happened to be an exact contiguous phrase, which is exactly why the naive model looked accurate for 5 cycles. The predictions were right by accident of phrasing.
- **Tooling shipped**: `bin/store-rank --attr` now computes and prints the query's **token span** in our title (0 = contiguous), flags `LIKELY PROXIMITY DEMOTION` when span > 0 and rank > 20, and stamps every prediction with "VALID ONLY IF the new title spells this query contiguously". The span helper scores the *tightest* occurrence, not the first — a first draft got this wrong and reported span 3 for `steam api` on a title that ranks p2 (the second "Steam" is the one Algolia scores). Fixed and re-verified against 3 known ground truths: span 0 -> p2/p2/p6, span 2 -> p128. CAVEAT 2 added to `attr()`'s docstring with the experiment table.

- **Tried to verify all 5 with cycle 522's "check raw `_highlightResult`" rule and got 5 apparent false positives (matchLevel "none" on our own hit) — then caught that this contradicted the two ALREADY-CONFIRMED real wins from cycles 520/522** (`recruitee`, `tmview`), which ALSO show matchLevel "none" on our own hit despite being proven real. Root-caused it: **Algolia only computes real `_highlightResult` for the first 6 hits of any query, confirmed by re-requesting the same query at hitsPerPage 3/20/100** — position 7+ is hard-coded "none" regardless of actual content (even for a hit whose title is byte-identical to a position-3 hit showing "full"). Checking OUR hit is therefore useless pre-edit, since we're never in the top 6 before the edit works. This also means cycle 522's "clinicaltrials.gov is a confirmed false positive" verdict was reached the same broken way — re-checked this cycle: a genuine title-match block DOES exist for that query (other developers score real matchLevel "full" at p1), our own non-participation in it is a separate, still-unexplained anomaly, not proof the block is fake.

Re-verified against ground truth: `recruitee`/`tmview` (known-real) now verify clean; all 5 of this cycle's new candidates ALSO verify as genuine blocks. Docstring corrected to document the p6 cutoff and retract the overbroad cycle-522 generalization.

Inbox unchanged from cycle 519 — no new mail, no owner reply on either the h137 visibility email or the h138 correction. 3 services active, site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`. - **All 21 Actors confirmed indexed in the buyer-facing Algolia index** (enumerated directly, not sampled) — cycle 518's "18" was the size of `bin/store-rank`'s `TERMS` map, not the indexed count. No visibility problem remains; this closes out the h137/h138 thread.

Measured ~11 candidate queries each and added the 3-4 winners per Actor with their measured rank in a trailing comment. They are our **best-placing Actors**: `super pac` p5, `fec api` p6, `docket scraper` p6, `tmview` p5, `euipo` p12, `fec filings` p12. Fleet scan is now 21/21, top-20 on 6/21 primary queries.
- **The real finding — the cycle-168 ranking model was wrong, and it was wrong in a direction that mattered.** Cycle 168 concluded "text relevance is maxed; rewriting titles/descriptions cannot move us; only `storePosition` matters," and every cycle since has treated rank as unactionable. Algolia evaluates its `attribute` criterion (which field the match landed in) **before** the custom `storePosition` tiebreaker, so a title match beats a description-only match regardless of `storePosition`. Proven on ONE record with `storePosition` held constant at 52702: `court-records-scraper` is **p67** on `courtlistener` (in our description only, and ranks 1..47 are precisely the 47 records with it in their *title*) but **p6** on `docket scraper` (both words in our title), ahead of competitors with `storePosition` 15715/32147/50062. 61 ranks, from text placement alone.
- **Did NOT edit any title this cycle — deliberately, and the tooling is why.** Added `bin/store-rank --attr "<query>" <slug>`, which reports whether we are outside the query's title-match block and what joining it would actually buy. For `courtlistener` it predicts p67 → ~p32 (31 title-matchers already have a better `storePosition`), i.e. still off page 1 and not worth burning the title real estate that currently wins us `docket scraper` p6. The point of the diagnostic is to make title edits a measured decision rather than a guess; the queries where it *will* pay are ones with small title-match blocks. Verified `--attr` on 3 cases: outside-block, already-in-block, and not-matching-at-all (exits 1).
- **`storePosition` 999999 is a "not yet scored" sentinel, not a penalty** — `trademark-search-scraper` (published this morning) has it on both `storePosition` and `experimentalStorePosition` while all 20 older Actors carry real values (51067-54480), including one published 2 days earlier. Re-measure after ~48h. It ranks p5 on `tmview` anyway.
- **Third instance of one recurring class of bug**: a standalone per-Actor tool that the publish flow never wires itself into (cycle 515 search index, cycle 519 site icons, now cycle 520 rank tracking). `TERMS` registration is now an explicit step in PLAYBOOK step 8, alongside the icon step.

## Cycle 517 (2026-09-19, sonnet-5, ~25min, GROWTH/CRITICAL FINDING) — SUPERSEDED, see cycle 518 above for the correction. root-caused the entire business's zero-revenue problem: Apify Store search excludes our whole account from anonymous/public results. Emailed owner (rule 3b: critical, only they can fix). 0 code shipped, 0 spend, 1 owner email sent.
- `date -u` FIRST: 20:00Z. No date gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z; `fda-recall-scraper` re-measurement needs >=2026-09-20 16:05Z). Inbox unchanged known-noise set, no reply owed. 3 services active, git clean. $0 spend.
- **Picked up cycle 516's suggested GROWTH/distribution thread and ran `bin/store-visibility` (written cycle 116, anonymous-only check) — still reports invisible, contradicting cycle 452's LEARNINGS claim that "the blackout is over".** Investigated the contradiction instead of trusting either note.
- **Root cause found, with hard proof, not inference.** `bin/check-store-rank` (written cycle 452, used for every rank measurement since — h50 through h136) sends `Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN` on every Store search call. That means **every "rank #X" measurement for ~65 cycles has measured what the authenticated owner account sees, never what a real anonymous buyer sees.** Direct proof, reproduced independently with plain curl (no wrapper script):
  - `curl "https://api.apify.com/v2/store?limit=100&search=fetchsmith"` (anonymous) -> 0 of our 21 Actors appear, even though the API's own match count claims 33-34.
  - Same call `+&includeUnrunnableActors=true` -> all 21 appear immediately.
  - `GET /v2/users/me` (authenticated, our own token) shows `effectivePlatformFeatures.ACTORS_PUBLIC_ALL.isEnabled: false`, `disabledReason: "The 'All public Actors' feature isn't enabled for your account. Please upgrade your plan or contact support@apify.com"`. `ACTORS_PUBLIC_DEVELOPER.isEnabled: true` (why the owner-token checks looked fine). Current plan: custom $1/mo Bronze tier, not Starter+.
  - Cross-checked against Apify's own docs (`docs.apify.com/api/v2/store-get`, fetched live): "By default, search results exclude Actors that are not safe to run automatically (e.g. Actors from developers who haven't passed KYC, or full-permission Actors without a large user base)." Matches exactly.
  - Control: `apify.com/fetchsmith` (our public profile page) DOES render our Actors (SSR-confirmed via curl) — so direct links / our own site work fine. Only Store SEARCH (the primary buyer discovery path) is affected.
- **This is the single most plausible explanation for $0 revenue and `totalUsers` stuck at platform-baseline `2` across all 21 Actors** (the exact anomaly cycle 516 flagged as unexplained). No amount of niche selection, pricing, README quality, or copy-editing (h108-h130's whole rank-experiment thread) could have mattered if buyers structurally cannot find any listing via search.
- **Emailed owner** (`bin/notify --once store_search_visibility_gate_2026-09-19`, sent 200 OK) — this is a rule-3(b) case: fixing it needs either a support request only the account owner can credibly make, or a paid plan upgrade (~$29/mo Starter) which needs explicit budget approval per rule 4. Did not add a budget line or take any account action myself. Did not overclaim: email states plainly this could be a free support-ticket fix (KYC/verification) or could need a paid upgrade — genuinely unknown from outside, owner needs to ask Apify directly.
- **NOT yet fixed: `bin/check-store-rank` and `bin/store-rank` still authenticate, so every future rank measurement using them remains misleading until patched.** Deliberately did not rewrite it this cycle (ran out of time budget after the investigation + email) — flagged as the top item for next cycle.
- **Verified**: 3 services active, git status clean (no repo changes this cycle — investigation only, one file written to `state/` and removed after sending). No Actor runs, no builds, no publishes, $0 spend.
- **Next cycle**: `date -u` FIRST. No date gates due yet. **Top priority: fix `bin/check-store-rank`/`bin/store-rank` to query anonymously (strip the `Authorization` header, or add an explicit `--as-public` mode) so the fleet's rank data reflects reality** — re-run the fleet-wide scan once fixed and expect very different (likely much worse) numbers than `state/store_rank.json`'s existing snapshots, which should be annotated or superseded as measuring the wrong thing. Correct the cycle-452 LEARNINGS entry claiming "the blackout is over" — it wasn't wrong about that moment's mechanics understanding, just used a token-authenticated check that couldn't see the real answer. Do NOT act further on the Apify support/plan-upgrade question until the owner replies — this was an email-and-wait item, not an open task to keep pushing on. If the owner hasn't replied, resume normal QUALITY/BUILD rotation per h136's notes (GROWTH angle: converting real google.com-referred site traffic, `bin/traffic` buyer-intent funnel still nowhere near the >100/day gate).

## Cycle 515 (2026-09-19, sonnet-5, ~15min, QUALITY/TOOLING — found and fixed a real Store search-index staleness bug that would have invalidated the pending `fda-recall-scraper` rank experiment) — 0 stale fields fleet-wide after 2 forced rebuilds. No code changed.
- `date -u` FIRST: 19:00Z. No date gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z; `fda-recall-scraper` store-rank re-measurement needs >=2026-09-20 16:05Z, still ~21h away). Inbox byte-identical to cycle 514's 10 newest — no reply owed, no owner email. 3 services active, git clean before starting (only cron-managed `revenue*.json`). $0 spend beyond existing Apify platform-usage credit.
- **All 6 standing checks ran clean first** (source-bytes 366/0, code-fields 0 drift, registry-fields 0 drift, store-meta 21/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 21/26/0).
- **Ran `bin/check-competitor-claims`** (not run in many cycles per cycle 514's note) — clean, 0 stale (0 user-count claims, 9 competitor paragraphs all dated/fresh).
- **Ran `bin/check-store-index`** (also not run in many cycles) and it found a real, live bug: **4 stale fields across 2 Actors in the Apify Store's Algolia search index.** `fda-recall-scraper` — `title`/`description`/`seoTitle` still indexed as the OLD pre-cycle-509 copy ("FDA Recall Scraper", singular) despite the live Actor record having carried the new "FDA Recalls Scraper" copy for ~3 hours. `court-records-scraper` — `description` still said "38 flat fields" despite the live record saying "39" since cycle 504. Per the script's own docstring: the search index is a **build-time snapshot** (`taggedBuilds.latest.finishedAt`), not the live Actor record — `apify-admin publish` updates the live page but does NOT itself push new text into search, so listing text can stay stale in search results indefinitely, and **"any Store-ranking / keyword-membership probe is meaningless until this reports 0 stale fields for the Actor in question."**
- **Why this mattered right now, not just in general**: cycle 509 changed `fda-recall-scraper`'s title specifically to test whether title-phrase-match moves Store rank, with a re-measurement explicitly queued for >=2026-09-20 16:05Z (h129/h134). Had this gone unnoticed, that re-measurement would have been checking the OLD stale-indexed title's rank against the NEW title's rank claim — the experiment's entire signal would have been unreadable, and a plausible real rank change could have been wrongly attributed to (or wrongly denied to) the copy edit.
- **Fixed with zero code changes**: `apify push --force -w 600` on both `fda-recall-scraper` (build 0.1.20) and `court-records-scraper` (build 0.1.18) — no source diff, just forces Apify to rebuild from the unchanged, already-correct source, which re-triggers Algolia reindexing. Re-ran `check-store-index` after a 30s wait: **0 stale fields fleet-wide** (was 4, across 2/21 Actors). Re-ran all 6 standing checks clean again post-push (source-bytes 366/0, code-fields/registry-fields 0 drift, store-meta 21/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 21/26/0) — confirms neither rebuild introduced drift. Site verified 200 on `/`, `/tools/fda-recall-scraper`, `/tools/court-records-scraper`; 3 services active; git tree clean except cron-managed `revenue*.json`.
- **New durable lesson for LEARNINGS**: after ANY `apify-admin publish` (metadata-only title/description/seoTitle/seoDescription change, no code diff), immediately follow with `apify push --force` on that Actor (or run `bin/check-store-index` fleet-wide) to force the search index to pick up the new copy — otherwise the change is live on the Actor's own Store page but invisible to Store *search*, silently, for an unbounded time. This should become a standing step appended to the "Store-ranking experiment" playbook pattern (h129-style copy-change-then-remeasure cycles), not just a one-off fix.
- Money: unchanged, **21 public Actors**, 42 users, $0 booked this cycle. No new Actors today.
- **Next cycle**: `date -u` FIRST. Date gates unchanged: dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z; `fda-recall-scraper` store-rank re-measurement eligible at >=2026-09-20 16:05Z (do the math from wall-clock — now genuinely trustworthy since the index is fresh as of this cycle, but re-run `check-store-index fda-recall-scraper` once more right before that measurement in case another metadata edit slips in between). This was QUALITY/TOOLING -> next non-gate cycle is a fair BUILD slot (fresh niche scan needed, pre-filter HTTP/JSON-only, skip the long closed-negative list in queue.md h50-h134/queue_archive.md) or another QUALITY pass (candidates: TMview proxy-502 flakiness watch item from cycle 514 if it recurs; `trademark-search-scraper` still too new for `bin/varied-test`, give it another day; add the "publish then force-push to reindex" step to PLAYBOOK/LEARNINGS properly if not done yet).

- **The cycle's real work: `bin/check-store-rank` was lying.** `GET /v2/store?search=` returns **73-93 items for `limit=100`** — it applies the limit and then drops filtered (deprecated/private) listings from the page it already cut. The tool treated a short page as the last page (`if len(items) < PAGE: break`), so it stopped after page 1 on essentially every query; and it computed rank as `offset + i`, which over-states position by the accumulated page shortfall. **Every "NOT IN TOP 300 / NOT IN TOP 1200" this tool has printed since cycle 452 actually meant "not in the first ~80 results".** Pages themselves are fine — offset IS honoured and pages are disjoint (verified: page@0 ∩ page@100 = 0 items for 'clinical trials'); they are just short.
- **Verified the fix against independent ground truth before trusting it**: wrote a throwaway exhaustive scanner first, which put `substack-scraper` at 88 for 'substack' and `google-play-reviews-scraper` at 109 for 'android app reviews'; the patched tool then reproduced 88 and 109 exactly.
- **Corrected distribution picture.** Actors previously believed invisible are merely deep: `shopify-products-scraper` #91 ('shopify products') / #280 ('shopify store'), `app-store-reviews-scraper` #93, `google-play-reviews-scraper` #96 / #109, `substack-scraper` #88, `google-news-scraper` #114 / #325, `hacker-news-scraper` #143 / #100, `ats-jobs-scraper` #404 / #495, `federal-register-scraper` #333, `grants-gov-scraper` #126, `steam-reviews-scraper` #87. **Exactly one genuine absence remains in the whole fleet: `substack-scraper` <- 'newsletter scraper'** (scanned all 1022 returned). The 11 page-1 rankings and the 11 near-miss queries (rank 25-52) are unchanged by the fix — it changes the diagnosis, not the standing.
- **Also fixed the misleading `of {total}` denominator.** The API's `total` runs ~20-25% above what search actually hands out (claims 1225 matches for 'substack', returns 981; claims 548 for 'android app reviews', returns 483). Never quote it as a rank denominator. Duplicates across pages do occur, so deep ranks are approximate. Snapshot schema gained `scanned`.
- **`state/store_rank.json` caveat**: snapshots 1-9 carry the buggy ranks. **Do not trend across the cycle-508 boundary**; the first trustworthy full-fleet snapshot is the 12th.
- **Verified**: all 6 standing checks clean (source-bytes 354/0, code-fields 0 drift, registry-fields 0 drift, store-meta 20/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 20/25/0). 3 services active, site 200 on `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`, `/tools/substack-scraper`. Read-only Apify Store API calls only, no Actor runs, no builds, 0 publish slots, $0 spend, 0 new Actors, no owner email (no revenue event).
- Money: unchanged, **$0 booked**, 20 public Actors, 40 users, 185 runs/30d (184 ok / 1 bad), 0 bookmarks, 0 reviews.

This was QUALITY/TOOLING -> next non-gate cycle is a fair BUILD slot (pre-filter: plain HTTP/JSON, no headless browser, AND not already in `ls actors/`). **Strongest follow-up**: distribution is now measured honestly and 11 queries sit at rank 25-52, one listing-copy change from page 1. Nothing is known about what Apify search ranks on. Run the first controlled experiment — change ONE Actor's title/description (pick a cheap near-miss such as `grants.gov` #37 or `fda recalls` #39), spend the one publish slot, re-run `check-store-rank` the following cycle against the clean baseline, and see whether rank moves. ## Cycle 488 (2026-09-19, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY — executes h107(a)/h106's hand-triage) — `court-records-scraper`'s 11 low-fill fields triaged against 240 live upstream rows: no code bug, but a real README overclaim found and closed. Build 0.1.10 live and platform-verified.
- `date -u` FIRST: 05:30Z. No gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z). Nightly health 19/20 — only the known `scholarship-scraper` bold.org block (h78/h101), no new signal, so nothing outranked the rotation. Inbox (8 newest) unchanged known-noise classes (3 GOV.UK/Companies House OTP artifacts, 3 dmarc, `helpindex.org` SEO spam, `drummondduana` cold pitch). No reply, no owner email. 486 QUALITY / 487 BUILD → 488 is a fair QUALITY slot, and h107 named the field-fill triage as the top candidate.
- **Method that made this work (new, reusable):** h106's `bin/check-field-fill` reads *our own* dataset rows, so on a multi-mode Actor its output is mode-clustered noise. Instead of reasoning from those 30 rows I went to the **upstream API directly** — 12 deliberately varied `api/rest/v4/search/?type=o` slices (different courts: `scotus`/`ca9`/`ca2`/`cafc`/`ny`/`tex`/`ill`/`ohio`/`cal`/`nd`, different date windows, different queries), 240 rows, anonymous, **$0 and no Actor runs**. That separates "null by design", "slice-dependent" and "never populated" in one pass.
- **Verdict: no code bug.** 3 of the 11 (`cause`, `juryDemand`, `chapter`) are hardcoded `null` on the opinion side at `src/main.js:421-425` — docket-only columns in the deliberate one-superset schema, so 0% on opinion-mode runs is correct. The other 8 are honest passthroughs of keys CourtListener's search index returns on every row but leaves empty unless the court supplied a value.
- **Measured fill, 240 upstream rows:** `neutralCite` 25%, `judge` 16%, `syllabus` 12%, `panelNames` 4%, `lexisCite` 2%, `proceduralHistory` 2/240, `posture` **0/240**, `court_jurisdiction` 21/240. `panel_ids` came back at the identical 4% as `panel_names`, which rules out a name-resolution bug — the data is simply absent. **The key finding is that the distribution is court-dependent, not random**: `ohioctapp`/`ill` gave `syllabus`+`neutralCite` on 20/20 while `ca9`/`ca2`/`ny`/`scotus` gave none. These are not dead fields; they are fields a buyer must choose a court for.
- **The actual defect was the listing, not the code.** "What you get" sold "posture, procedural history, syllabus" as ordinary opinion-row content while `posture` was empty on every row we could find. Also: `jurisdictionType` is PACER readable text on dockets (`"Diversity"`) but a raw one-letter court code (`"F"`) on opinions and null on ~91% — and the "Docket analytics" use case cited it without saying it was docket-side.
- **Shipped (build 0.1.10, README-only, `src/` untouched):** opinions bullet now names the six editorial extras as minority-fill and points at limitations; two new **Honest limitations** bullets carry the measured percentages, the court-dependence finding, concrete advice (filter `courts` to a court that publishes it, check a small run first) and the reassurance that empty fields don't change the $0.002/row charge; "Docket analytics" qualified as `recordType: "dockets"`.
- **Verified**: `apify push --force` → build **0.1.10**, `latest` tag confirmed; the live build's own `actorDefinition.readme` re-fetched (16898 bytes) with both new bullets present. Real platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items` (`negligence`/`opinions`/`filedAfter 2020-01-01`/5) → **201, 5 rows, 39 fields**, and the rows independently confirm the README's claims (`nd`/`connappct`/`ncctapp`/`ohioctapp` all `syllabus` non-null, `neutralCite` 3/5, `posture` and `jurisdictionType` null 5/5). All 6 standing checks clean (source-bytes 353/0, code-fields 0, registry-fields 0, store-meta 20/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 20/25/0). 3 services active, 4 site paths 200 (`/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/tools/court-records-scraper`). $0 spend, 0 new Actors.

## Cycle 486 (2026-09-19, sonnet-5, QUALITY — executed h105(d)'s idea) — shipped `bin/check-field-fill`, a fleet-wide null-rate audit for declared output fields; ran it, found no new bug, logged an important limitation.
- `date -u` FIRST: ~04:50Z. No gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z). Inbox (10 newest) re-checked: same known-noise classes as prior cycles — owner's `13e16bd5` icon-thread is already fully closed (icons shipped cycle 364/465), `aleksandrlugeza` i18n cold pitch, 3 GOV.UK/Companies House OTP artifacts, 3 dmarc, `helpindex.org` SEO spam, `drummondduana` cold pitch. No reply needed, no owner email.
- **Built** `bin/check-field-fill`: reuses `check-real-fields`' existing recent-SUCCEEDED-runs fetch (no new runs, $0 cost) and reports what fraction of real dataset rows have each `dataset_schema.json`-declared field non-null/non-empty. This is the check that would have caught cycle 485's `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` `deadlineDate` bug on its own.
- **Ran fleet-wide**: 19 actors checked, 263 fields flagged below 30% fill. Manually verified the 3 largest offenders (`steam-reviews-scraper`, `fec-campaign-finance-scraper`, `google-play-reviews-scraper`) are **not bugs** — each Actor has a `dataType`/mode input, and the last 3 sampled SUCCEEDED runs all happened to share one mode, so the other mode's fields are correctly null (confirmed against each README's own documented mode split).
- **Limitation found and logged**: fill-rate is only trustworthy computed *within* a mode. The script doesn't yet bucket by each Actor's mode param (name not standardized across the fleet: `dataType`, `mode`, etc.) before computing rates, so on any multi-mode Actor it will flag real, expected fields as long as recent runs cluster in one mode. Documented in LEARNINGS and in the script's own docstring/usage note — treat its output as a **candidate list to hand-triage**, never a pass/fail gate.
- **No new bug shipped this cycle** (unlike cycle 485). Left precisely noted in h106/queue.md: hand-triage the remaining ~250 flagged lines in future QUALITY cycles, one Actor at a time; two unconfirmed candidates worth a first look are `court-records-scraper` (`syllabus`/`panelNames`/`chapter`/`posture`/`proceduralHistory` all 0%) and `federal-register-scraper` (`significant` 10%).
- All standing checks re-run clean, 3 services active (`fetchsmith-web`/`fetchsmith-mail`/`caddy`), 3 site paths 200 (`/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`). $0 spend, 0 new Actors, no Actor code touched (tooling-only cycle), no owner email. ## Cycle 485 (2026-09-19, opus-5, BUILD/competitor-gap audit — first audit in five to find a REAL gap, and it uncovered a bigger data-quality bug) — `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` gains deadline filtering, and its `deadlineDate` field stops being null on 95% of rows. Build 0.1.19 live and platform-verified.
- `date -u` FIRST: 04:00Z. No gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z). Inbox (8 newest) unchanged known-noise classes (3 dmarc, 3 GOV.UK/Companies House OTP artifacts, `helpindex.org` SEO spam, `drummondduana` cold pitch) — no reply, no owner email. Nightly health 19/20: only the known `scholarship-scraper` bold.org block (h78/h101), so no new health signal outranked the rotation; 482 BUILD, 483 FIX, 484 QUALITY → 485 is a fair BUILD slot, and `eu-ted-tenders`/`fec-campaign-finance` were the queued stalest audits.
- **Niche sizes (fresh `apify-admin store`)**: "eu tenders" has grown — `artificially/eu-tenders-scraper` 39 users, `foxlabs/ted-tenders` 36 (11 u30d, most active), `memo23` 16, `maximedupre` 15, ~7 smaller. "campaign finance" leader `ryanclinton/fec-campaign-finance` only 16 users, long tail of 2-user clones. We appear in **neither** result list (same store-visibility problem as h97).
- **Gap found (input axis)**: the 39-user leader offers `onlyOpenDeadlines` + `minDaysUntilDeadline`; we had **no deadline filter at all** on an Actor whose README sells "deadline tracking". Its other extras (`includeBuyerProfile`/`includeFullDetails`/`includeSimilarTenders`) are enrichment we deliberately don't do; `minEstimatedValue`/`maxEstimatedValue` we already ship as `minValue`/`maxValue`. Output axis: no gap. **Pricing: we remain cheapest** — $0.003/result flat, no start fee, vs `foxlabs` $0.004 + $0.00005 start and `artificially` $0.003 tiered **plus** a $0.07-$0.10-per-GB start event.
- **The bigger find, hit while testing the new filter**: `deadlineDate` read TED's `deadline-date-lot`, the rarest of TED's three deadline fields. Measured live on 10 fresh FRA `cn-standard` notices: `deadline-receipt-tender-date-lot` present on **9**, `deadline-date-lot` on **1**; a 20-row stock run had `deadlineDate` null on **19/20**. We were advertising a use case on a field that was almost always empty, and no existing check could see it (all 6 compare field *names*, never *fill rate*). Fixed with a preference order (tender-receipt → generic → expressions-of-interest) plus a new `deadlineType` naming the source. **Fill rate 1/20 → 16/20**; the 4 remaining nulls are `can-standard` award notices, which genuinely have no deadline.
- **Shipped in 0.1.19**: inputs `onlyOpenDeadlines` + `minDaysUntilDeadline` (post-fetch, like `minValue`/`maxValue` — `deadline-date-lot` is a per-lot array, so a server-side comparison would match a notice on ANY lot); output `deadlineType` + `daysUntilDeadline` (whole days UTC, negative = closed, null = none published); zero-result status message names only the filter(s) that actually dropped rows (cycles 483/484 rule). Both new inputs stay OUT of the watch-mode fingerprint — `onlyOpenDeadlines` is time-varying, same trap as rolling `publishedWithinDays` (cycles 297/298).
- **Verified**: `node --check`; stock local run unchanged 20/20; fill rate measured before and after; `onlyOpenDeadlines`+`minDaysUntilDeadline: 14` → 20 rows all ≥16 days out, 12 dropped and logged, none charged; `minDaysUntilDeadline: 9999` → walked all 13 pages, 0 rows, 0 charged, honest "3247 dropped by onlyOpenDeadlines/minDaysUntilDeadline" status message. `apify push --force` → build **0.1.19**; real platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with both new filters → 201, 5/5 rows, every row `deadlineType: tender` at 17-23 days out, 27 fields. registry.json (output_fields, summary) + README (use case, both tables, sample row) updated; site restarted, `/tools/eu-ted-tenders-scraper` renders all three new names, 5 paths 200, 3 services active. All 6 standing checks clean (source-bytes 352/0, code-fields 0, registry-fields 0, store-meta 20/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 20/25/0). **$0 spend, 0 new Actors, no owner email.**
- **Reusable trick (now in LEARNINGS)**: to enumerate a TED field name instead of guessing, POST `/v3/notices/search` with a bogus `fields: ["zzz"]` — the 400 body lists every supported field; `grep -i deadline` over it returned 19 candidates and found all three variants.
- **Left for next cycle (h105)**: (a) Store short description still doesn't mention the deadline filter — the differentiator a buyer sees before clicking; needs `apify-admin publish`, which burns a publication slot, so it was not worth rushing at cycle end. (b) `registry.json sample_output` here is an award notice with all three deadline fields null — accurate but a weak shop window now. (c) `fec-campaign-finance-scraper` audit scoped but not executed, now the stalest. (d) **New standing idea**: sweep the fleet for output fields that are declared and advertised but null on most real rows — same defect class as this one, invisible to all 6 checks.
- **Next cycle**: 486 should be QUALITY per the every-3rd rule; cheapest high-value items are h104's residual (first-page `break` shape in `substack`/`ats-jobs`/`hacker-news`, one batched fix) or (a)/(b) above.

## Cycle 483 (2026-09-19, opus-5, ~20min, FIX — real bug shipped) — `shopify-products-scraper` was calling a live 250-product store "empty / products.json disabled" off ONE transient empty response. Build 0.1.40 live and platform-verified.
- `date -u` FIRST: 03:00Z. No gates due (dev.to slot 7 ~2026-09-21 00:06Z; h74/h99/h78 all closed). Inbox (5 newest) same known-noise classes (3 dmarc, `helpindex.org` SEO spam, `drummondduana` cold pitch) — no reply, no owner email.
- **Target choice**: the nightly health check (02:33Z) flagged TWO Actors — `scholarship-scraper` (the known bold.org bot-block, closed at h78/h101) and **`shopify-products-scraper`, which had never been unhealthy before** (cycle 481 recorded scholarship-scraper as the fleet's only unhealthy Actor). A genuinely new failure signal outranks the QUALITY rotation, so this cycle was a FIX cycle.
- **Root cause — a class of bug no existing retry layer catches.** Failing run `Joxfa1M1UlO4qUU4y` (02:33:48Z) received a real **HTTP 200 carrying `{"products":[]}`** from `allbirds.com/products.json?limit=250&page=1` and treated that single response as definitive truth. It is not an exception, not a non-2xx, and not a parse error, so the fleet's 429/5xx + network-error `try/catch` hardening (cycles 442/h68) passes straight over it. The run SUCCEEDS, charges $0, and hands the buyer a confident wrong diagnosis (`products.json is disabled`) about a storefront they know works.
- **Alternatives disproved before touching code**: the store's 3 previous runs (01:01Z, 02:01Z, 09-18 14:03Z, same input) each returned 10 rows; direct curl from this box returned 250 products at both `limit=5` and `limit=250`; and **3 separate Apify Proxy sessions each returned 250 products** — so not proxy-IP blocking, not a `limit=250`/`page`-param deprecation, not a code regression. Transient Shopify edge behaviour (stale empty page cache, or a rate-limited datacenter IP answered 200-with-nothing instead of 429).
- **Fix (build 0.1.40)**: zero-products-on-page-1 of a store/collection is re-confirmed up to 2 more times (2s/4s backoff) before being believed; each attempt gets a fresh proxy IP for free because `proxyUrlFor()` is already called per request with no session id. Later pages untouched (running out there is legitimate). The empty-store warning now says "on 3 separate attempts" — but only for the paged route, since the single-product route makes no retries and must not assert them.
- **Verified**: `node --check`; stock local run 10/10 rows unchanged; **both fault polarities** injected via a disposable `src/main.fault.js` copy (main.js never edited, so no restore step to forget) — always-empty → 3 attempts, honest message, 0 rows, 0 charged; **empty-once → recovers to 10 rows, i.e. the exact health-check failure now self-heals**. `apify push` → build 0.1.40, then a real platform `run-sync-get-dataset-items` on `test_input.json` → 201, 10 items, fields intact. All 6 standing checks clean (source-bytes 352/0, code-fields 0, registry-fields 0, store-meta 20/0, meta-fields 8/0, pricing 20/25/0), 3 services active, 5 site paths 200 (incl. `/tools/shopify-products-scraper`). $0 spend, 0 new Actors.
- **New follow-up for a QUALITY slot**: audit the rest of the fleet for this same defect shape — a bare `if (!items.length) break;` on the *first* page of a paged source, i.e. anywhere an empty-but-valid 200 is accepted as proof of "no data" without re-confirmation, plus zero-result messages that assert a cause the code never verified. See h103 in queue.md.

## Cycle 472 (2026-09-18, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY — 471 was BUILD, per its own next-step note) — `apple-podcasts-scraper`: found and fixed a real cross-source bug via a first-ever varied-input sweep — the RSS path reported every episode `explicit:false` when a feed carries no per-episode tag, silently emptying `explicitFilter:"explicitOnly"`. Build 0.1.28 live. Also first varied-test sweeps for `app-store-reviews-scraper` and `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` (both clean).
- `date -u` FIRST: 21:30Z. **Neither gate due** — h74 rank verdict needs >=2026-09-19 00:00Z (~2.5h out), dev.to slot 6 needs >=00:06Z. Inbox (10 newest) byte-identical known-noise classes to cycle 471. No reply, no owner email.

- **`app-store-reviews-scraper` — clean.** Notion, `minRating:1`+`maxRating:2`+`minReviewLength:120`: 8/8 rows rated 1-2 (Notion skews 5-star, so a silently-ignored rating filter would have been obvious), and the two borderline rows measured 127 and 123 chars — consistent with `content.trim().length >= 120` at `src/main.js:86`, not an off-by-one or a title+content count.
- **`uk-find-a-tender-scraper` — clean.** FTS/tender/`buyerName:"NHS"`/`minValueGbp:1000000`/90d: 6/6 rows NHS buyers, values GBP 1.2M-137.7M, all within the window.
- **`apple-podcasts-scraper` — REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED.** Same episode came back `explicit:true` from Apple's lookup API and `explicit:false` from the RSS path, so `explicitFilter:"explicitOnly"` + `useRssForFullArchive:true` returned **0 rows** on a show Apple rates Explicit. Root cause at `rssEpisodeRow`: `explicit` was `['yes','true','explicit'].includes(<itunes:explicit> text)`, i.e. an **absent** tag read as a definite "not explicit". Measured on the real feed: Lex Fridman's feed has **0 per-episode `<itunes:explicit>` tags across all 503 items** (448/503 carry `<itunes:duration>`), and declares `false` at channel level, while Apple's per-episode `contentAdvisoryRating` says `Explicit` and its *collection* explicitness says `notExplicit` — three sources, two disagreements, on one of the best-known podcasts.
  - **Fix**: new `parseItunesExplicit()` returns `null` for an absent tag (not `false`), so the row now resolves item-level -> channel-level -> `false`; both RSS entry points (`scrapeRssFeed` for Apple-ID shows, `scrapeEpisodesFromFeed` for pasted feed URLs) now pass the channel flag through. Added a run-log warning (same warn-don't-silently-mislead pattern as the existing `minDurationSeconds`/`minVoteSum` warnings) that fires when `explicitFilter` is set and N items had no per-episode tag, telling the buyer the show-level flag was used and to turn RSS off to filter on Apple's rating instead.
  - **Verified both polarities locally** (channel-level fallback cannot be exercised by any real feed found that also lacks item tags, so served two variants of the real 2.1 MB Lex feed over `127.0.0.1:8899`): channel `yes` -> 3/3 rows `explicit:true` kept by `explicitOnly` (pre-fix this was 0 rows); channel `false` -> 3/3 `explicit:false` kept by `clean`. Warning fired in both, citing 503 items.
  - **Platform-verified** build 0.1.28: Joe Rogan (feed has per-item tags on all 2753 items, the unchanged path) via `bin/varied-test` -> 4/4 `explicit:true`, `source:"rss"` — no regression on the common case.
  - **Docs**: `explicitFilter`'s input-schema description (the Console-visible surface) now says which source the flag comes from and that the two can disagree; README row carries the measured Lex example and the date. Also folded in a second doc gap the sweep surfaced: `minDurationSeconds`' schema description never mentioned that Apple omits duration for a large share of episodes and those are kept — the README said it, the Console field did not.
- **Verified**: all 6 standing checks clean (`check-source-bytes` 351/0, `check-code-fields` 0, `check-registry-fields` 0, `check-readme-samples` 26+33/0, `check-store-meta` 20/0, `check-meta-fields` 8/0). 3 services active, `/`, `/tools`, `/pricing`, `/tools/apple-podcasts-scraper` all 200.

- **Output side: the real find, and it was an internal inconsistency, not just a competitor gap.** Their dataset view ships `primaryOutcomeMeasures`/`secondaryOutcomeMeasures`, `enrollmentType`, `standardAges`, inclusion/exclusion criteria and `centralContacts`; we shipped none of those. Checking our own schema against itself was sharper: **four advertised filters ranged over data we never emitted** — `outcomeMeasure` (searches `query.outc`), `ageGroups`, `resultsFirstPostedDateFrom/To`, and the ambiguity in `enrollmentCount`. A buyer could filter on an outcome or an age bucket and have nothing on the row confirming what matched.
- **Shipped 6 fields**, all from study JSON we already fetch (zero extra API requests, no pricing/filtering logic touched): `primaryOutcomes`/`secondaryOutcomes` (`measure`, `timeFrame`, `description` per endpoint), `standardAges`, `resultsFirstPostDate`, `enrollmentType` (ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED), `eligibilityCriteria`. 30 -> 36 declared fields (34 per row + 2 watch-mode).
- **Two judgment calls, both recorded in code comments so they don't get "fixed" later:** (1) outcome `description` is included because `query.outc` searches it too — verified live, 2 of 8 hits for `outcomeMeasure:"HbA1c"` matched ONLY in the description, so omitting it would leave those rows looking like false positives (median 114 chars, 132/170 outcomes sampled — cheap). (2) `eligibilityCriteria` ships as the registry's raw text and is deliberately NOT pre-split into inclusion/exclusion the way the competitor does: that split is a heuristic over free-form prose and mislabelling an exclusion criterion as an inclusion one is the one error a trial-screening buyer cannot afford. `centralContacts` stays dropped per the standing no-contact-PII rule — the competitor ships it, we will not.
- **Verified**: 3 local runs (stock `test_input.json` regression 12/12 rows, 0 filter violations, all new keys present; a `resultsAvailability:"with"`+`ageGroups:["CHILD"]`+`outcomeMeasure:"HbA1c"` run confirming 8/8 `resultsFirstPostDate` non-null and 8/8 `standardAges` containing CHILD; a re-run after adding `description` taking outcome-match explainability from 5/8 to 8/8) + build 0.1.22 pushed + 2 platform runs via `bin/varied-test` on an asthma/CHILD/FEV1 query: 5/5 rows CHILD-tagged, 5/5 with a real `resultsFirstPostDate`, 5/5 `enrollmentType:"ACTUAL"`, 5/5 with FEV1 visibly present in the emitted outcomes. (2) watch mode's "seen" set — `dateFiledAsc` walks oldest-first, so on an established watch label an incremental run can burn its whole page budget skipping long-delivered rows before reaching new ones near the recent end. Added a `log.warning` gated to non-seeding runs with `sortBy:"dateFiledAsc"`+`watchLabel` set. **Reproduced live**: seeded a throwaway watch label with ascending sort, re-ran immediately with zero new matches available, and the incremental run walked all 48 pages / 956 rows (the entire match set) before finishing — exactly the predicted wasted-effort shape, though never a billing risk since skipped rows are free.
- `sortBy` deliberately excluded from `watchCriteria` (the baseline fingerprint) — it reorders the same match set, never changes which records match, so switching it shouldn't discard an existing baseline (same convention as the eu-ted `minValue`/`maxValue` precedent). Also wired `order_by` into the `startUrl` paste-a-URL shortcut, same pattern as the other pasted fields (unrecognised value warns and falls back to the input field).

The real gap came from a small listing, `seibs.co/court-records-intel` (11 users): search by **party / attorney / case number** — the question a legal-data buyer actually asks, and the one our full-text `query` answers worst (a party search for "Google LLC" vs. full text that also matches every opinion merely *citing* Google).
- **Probed every candidate param live before writing code** — and the control mattered: a bogus param leaves the result count untouched, so "count unchanged" means "silently ignored". Real: `party_name "Google LLC"` 6,498 vs 2,110,970 RECAP baseline; `atty_name "Smith"` 65,978; `docket_number "1:20-cv-03590"` 6; `judge "Posner"` 8,411 on opinions.
- **The probe found a live billing trap, which shaped the whole design.** CourtListener does not reject a field the index can't honour — it ignores it: `type=o&party_name=…` returns **8,313,056** rows (the entire opinion corpus) because the only filter sent was dropped on the floor; `judge` on RECAP does the same (61.9M). Shipping the filters naively would have billed a buyer per row for an unfiltered corpus. So the Actor now **narrows the run to the index that carries the field** (`partyName`/`attorneyName` → dockets only, `judge` → opinions only, each with an explicit log line saying why the other half was skipped), **errors upfront** when a filter contradicts an explicit `recordType`, and **errors on `partyName`+`judge`** (no single index carries both, so it could never match). `docketNumber` works on both and is sent to both.
- **Verified**: 8 local runs (stock 12/12 unchanged; `partyName:"Google LLC"` 10/10 dockets all matching; `docketNumber` 6/6 exact; `judge:"Posner"` 8/8 opinions all Posner; startUrl carrying `party_name`+`atty_name` parsed and 6/6 matching both; all 3 guard cases throw before any HTTP request, 0 rows) + 3 platform runs on build 0.1.8 (stock 12/12 unchanged, party 10/10 dockets, judge 6/6 opinions). README (4 input rows, a new "Search by party, attorney, docket number or judge" section, startUrl param list) and `registry.json` summary updated; no output field changed → `check-code-fields`/`check-registry-fields` 0 drift, `meta.json` untouched (its description doesn't enumerate filters, same precedent as cycles 454/455) → **no publish slot spent**.

  - **Already safe, no gap** (confirmed by reading the code, not inferring from `retry:{limit:N}` alone): `steam-reviews-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`, `app-store-reviews-scraper`, `substack-scraper`, `hacker-news-scraper`, `fec-campaign-finance-scraper` — every per-item/per-page call site individually try/catch-wrapped with a graceful degrade (warn + null/skip/continue). `ats-jobs-scraper`'s 6 bare `getJson` call sites looked unwrapped at first glance but the per-company loop one level up already does `try { result = await FETCHERS[ats](slug) } catch (e) { erroredCompanies.push(...); continue; }` — a fetch failure for one company is already non-fatal.

Exact same bug class as h68, just living in a `for (const url of urls)` loop instead of a hand-rolled attempt-counter loop.
  - **Fix**: wrapped the per-URL `fetchHtml(url)` call in try/catch — a thrown error now logs `<url> — request failed (<message>), skipping this page.`, records the URL in a new `erroredUrls` list, and `continue`s to the next URL instead of failing the run; a summary warning lists all skipped URLs after the loop, matching the fleet's existing `erroredCompanies`/`notFoundCompanies` convention from `ats-jobs-scraper`. Build 0.1.13 live.
  - **Verified with the cycle-444 fault-injection recipe**: local run with `startUrls` = one real bold.org URL + one `http://127.0.0.1:9/dead-page/` (instant ECONNREFUSED) — the dead URL logged the new WARN and was skipped, the real URL's 16 scholarships were still pushed, and the run exited 0 ("Done. ## Cycle 442 (2026-09-18, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY) — `actor-health` (stale since cycle 434) caught a real live FAILED run on `court-records-scraper`; found and fixed the root cause, build 0.1.6 live. Found the same defect in 5 more Actors, queued as h68.
- `date -u` first: 06:30Z — dev.to slot 6 still not due (needs ≥2026-09-19 00:06Z). Per cycle 441's note, 442 is the due QUALITY cycle (every-3rd-cycle pace rule). Reviewed inbox (10 newest, all previously classified noise: owner's already-answered icon thread, cold i18n pitch, advance-fee scam, GOV.UK/Companies House OTP artifacts, 3 dmarc, 1 new SEO-spam "add to Google's index" pitch) — no reply, no owner email. - Ran the fleet-wide `bin/actor-health` sweep (last run cycle 434, 8 cycles / 7 builds stale) rather than another combinatorial-verification or competitor-gap pass, both of which were already exhausted per cycles 436/439. Result: 19/20 green, **`court-records-scraper` FAILED** (run `gUXbfnafB1CmKLbzA`, `status: FAILED`).
- **Root cause, found by reading the run's own log**: an unhandled `TimeoutError` (60s, network-level — not an HTTP status) against CourtListener's search endpoint crashed the Node process. `apiGet`'s hand-rolled retry loop (`for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 4; ...)`) only retries on HTTP status codes (429/5xx checked after the request resolves); with no `try/catch` around the `await gotScraping(...)` call itself, a network-level exception (timeout/ECONNRESET/DNS) propagates unhandled and kills the whole run. Confirmed transient — the identical input (`{"query":"trademark infringement","recordType":"both","courts":["ca9"],"maxResults":12}`) succeeded immediately on retry, both via a direct API call and after the fix — but the underlying code defect was real and will recur on any ordinary network blip.
- **Fix**: wrapped the `gotScraping` call in `try/catch`; a thrown error now retries with the same backoff as a 429/5xx (`log.warning`, `sleep`, `continue`) instead of crashing. This is the exact pattern already live and proven on `grants-gov-scraper`/`nih-reporter-scraper` (built post-cycle-421) — not a new design, a port of an existing fix.
- **Verified**: local regression unchanged (12 rows, matching cycle 423's baseline) both before and after the fix; pushed build 0.1.6; platform run on the exact stock `test_input.json` returned 10/10 rows (capped by `limit=10`), confirming no regression on the live build. No output-field change → `check-code-fields`/`check-registry-fields` both 0 drift (39/39), `check-source-bytes` 347/0. No README/schema/meta change needed (internal reliability fix, not a feature) → no publish slot spent.

Queued as h68 (queue.md) for a mechanical ~3-Actors-per-cycle port, same shape as h67's `webhookUrl` rotation. Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 442.

Everything was a subset (appIds/urls/searchQueries, start/endDate, review/purchase/sort filters, scrapeGameDetails) **except** `datawell`'s `includeOwnerEstimates`. Its `mode:"reviewSummary"` was a false-positive gap — our `dataType:"games"` row already returns the full `query_summary` **plus** store data, a strict superset.
- **The gap needed a third-party source:** Steam's own store API exposes neither owner counts nor crowd tags; SteamSpy (free, public, no login) does. Probed it live across 7 apps FIRST: `owners`, `ccu` and the 20-tag vote map populated on every one; **`average_forever`/`median_forever`/`*_2weeks` are a flat 0 on all 7** (dead since Valve hid profile playtime). My first guard (`appid == null`) passed that through, i.e. would have sold a made-up owner estimate for every app SteamSpy lacks. Can't just reject the `"0 .. 20,000"` string either — it's a legitimate bucket for genuinely tiny games (confirmed on two real Steam apps). Guard now keys on `name` being non-empty; missing data yields explicit nulls plus a run-log warning naming the App IDs.

Paced to SteamSpy's 1 req/sec limit, failures degrade the row instead of failing the run, **no new charging event** (fields ride the game row already paid for). Fields are spread conditionally so a flag-off row keeps its exact existing shape.
- Verified: 4 local runs (enriched 3/3 correct vs raw API; flag off = 33 keys unchanged; reviews mode + flag = correct warning, 39-key review rows untouched; two tiny real apps returning the legitimate `0 .. 20,000` bucket) + **3 platform runs on build 0.1.28** (Hades/Monster Hunter Wilds enriched 2/2 correct incl. tags that genuinely beat Steam's genres — Hades `Action Roguelike/Rogue-lite/Hack and Slash` vs `Action/Indie/RPG`; **default-input gate `{}` → 200 review rows, 39 keys, zero owner fields**). ## Cycle 430 (2026-09-18, sonnet-5, ~25min, BUILD/competitor-gap) — `substack-scraper` fresh diff found a real gap: shipped `leaderboardOnly`/`leaderboardTier`, build 0.1.24 live.

The cycle-400 dead end (cross-Substack keyword *search*, soft-blocked at the source) is unrelated and still correctly closed — this is a different Substack surface (public leaderboard pages, not search).
- **Live-verified the leaderboard API is public, unauthenticated JSON**, not the soft-blocked search: `substack.com/api/v1/category/public/<categoryId>/<all|free|paid>?page=&limit=` returns the exact same rich publication object our existing `includePublicationInfo`/`mapPublicationInfo()` already parses from a publication's homepage (`freeSubscriberCount`, `rankingDetail` paid-subscriber band, `author_name`/`bio`, Stripe `plans` with real prices) — confirmed live on `technology`/`paid` (SemiAnalysis #1, $50/mo–$500/yr) and `finance`/`free`. So a leaderboard hit doubles as a complete, zero-extra-request publication profile.
- **Shipped `leaderboardOnly` (boolean) + `leaderboardTier` (`all`/`free`/`paid`, also usable with normal `discoverCategories` scraping, not just leaderboard mode).** When `leaderboardOnly:true`, the Actor returns one `type:"leaderboard"` row per publication straight from the leaderboard response (`rank`, `category`, `leaderboardTier`, `name`, `handle`, `customDomain`, plus every `publication*` field) — zero post/comment scraping, charged on a new cheap `leaderboard-row` event ($0.0015 Free → $0.0005 Gold+, no Actor-start fee) instead of the post-text event. `easyapi`'s pricing is $0.00299/result **plus a $0.09 Actor-start fee** — this undercuts it at every tier with zero start fee.
- Reused `mapPublicationInfo()` unchanged (same raw Substack publication-object shape from both the homepage preload and the leaderboard API), so no new profile-parsing code — only a new discovery path and output mapper (`mapLeaderboardEntry`). `discoverPublications()` now returns `{found, entries}`: `found` still feeds the existing scrape path unchanged, `entries` carries rank + raw pub object for leaderboard-only mode. `rank` is the true leaderboard position (`page*pageSize + index + 1`), computed before the `discoverType` filter so it always matches what a human sees on `substack.com/leaderboard/<cat>/<tier>`.
- **Caught and fixed a self-inflicted false positive from `bin/check-code-fields` while verifying**: the pre-existing internal `found.push({..., name, category})` helper object (never pushed to the dataset) coincidentally gained 2-key overlap with the *new* dataset-schema fields `name`/`category` I'd just added, so the heuristic misidentified it as a dataset-row literal and flagged `origin`/`postSlug` as undeclared. Fixed by renaming the internal-only keys to `pubName` (not `postSlug`, which is a real dataset semantic elsewhere) — zero behavior change, confirmed via local regression before and after, `check-code-fields` back to 0 drift (59/60, `url` soft-flagged as before, pre-existing).
- Verified: 2 local regression runs (stock `test_input.json` unchanged 20 rows, both before and after the rename fix) + 3 local `leaderboardOnly` runs (`technology`/paid 5/5 correct incl. real Stripe prices, `finance`/free 5/5, bogus category → correct warn-and-empty, `leaderboardOnly` with no `discoverCategories` → correct warn-and-empty) + **3 platform runs on build 0.1.24** (`technology`/paid 3/3 rows byte-matching the local run incl. rank order; stock regression 20/20 rows unchanged, `post`+`comment` types only). No output-field regression — `publication*` fields identical to the existing post-row shape.
- Docs: README (2 new inputs, new "What's the difference between leaderboardOnly and discoverCategories+includePublicationInfo" FAQ, new `type:"leaderboard"` output section with a real sample, new pricing row, new use case). `registry.json output_fields` gained `rank`/`category`/`leaderboardTier`/`name`/`handle`/`customDomain` (60 fields now); `.actor/dataset_schema.json` synced; `meta.json`/`.actor/actor.json` description updated (mentions leaderboard rows + $0.0005 price) and republished via `apify-admin publish` (had to trim `seoTitle` to fit the 60-char API limit, caught by the publish call's own 400 error — not a silent truncation). Shared `minAmount`/`maxAmount`/`contributionDateFrom`/`contributionDateTo` now apply to whichever amount/date the mode uses; `watchLabel` works in all three transaction modes, with `searchMode` joining the fingerprint **only when not `contributions`** so pre-existing baselines keep their keys.

## Cycle 424 (2026-09-17, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD/competitor-gap) — `apple-podcasts-scraper` second pass: shipped `chartType` (Apple's Trending Episodes chart) + fixed a live `chartCount` cap bug, build 0.1.26 live.

Two competitors that did not exist at cycle 401's diff — `coder_zoro/apple-podcast-episodes-scraper` (65 users) and `coder_zoro/apple-podcast-top-chart-scrapper` (51, whose single input's enum includes "top episodes") — plus `sourabhbgp/apple-podcast-scraper`'s `trending-episodes` mode all pointed at the same gap. Their other extras are LLM-shaped, Spotify-credential passthrough, or filters we already have.
- **The gap:** `dataType:"charts"` only hit Apple's Top Shows feed (`.../podcasts/top/<n>/podcasts.json`). The same path with `podcast-episodes.json` serves a **separate "Trending Episodes" chart** (200 OK, verified live) — a different ranking, not a view of the shows chart: on 2026-09-17 US, #1 show = The Daily, while episode ranks 1-12 were episodes of 11 different shows. `podcast-channels.json` 404s (no third chart).
- **Method settled by measurement, not assumption:** an episode ID is not addressable in Apple's lookup API (`lookup?id=<episodeId>` → `resultCount:0`, with or without `entity=podcastEpisode`). The only route is looking up the parent SHOW (`entity=podcastEpisode&limit=200`) and matching `trackId` — one request per chart entry, cached per show (The Daily held 2 of the top 12 slots), and the same response carries the show record so show metadata costs nothing extra. 19/20 entries fully enriched; the miss was "Apple News Today", an Apple-exclusive show (`feedUrl:null`) that exposes no episode list. Unenriched entries still ship with the identical key rectangle, `source:"chart"`, and the chart's own title/artwork/URL — ranks never have holes from an upstream gap.
- **Real bug fixed in passing:** `chartCount` allowed up to 200, but the marketingtools endpoint **500s above 100** on both charts (probed 100 OK; 101/150/199/200 all 500), so `chartCount` 101-200 on the overall chart returned **0 rows** with only a warning. The older genre endpoint genuinely serves 200 (400s at 250). Cap is now per-endpoint (100 overall / 200 genre), warned when clamped.
- `chartGenre` is loudly dropped under `chartType:"episodes"` (no per-genre episode chart exists) instead of silently returning the overall chart. Episode filters apply to episode-chart rows before charging (ranks can gap by design), and the zero-rows diagnostic now names those filters with values rather than blaming "no valid podcast IDs".
- Verified 9 local + 3 platform runs on build 0.1.26 (stock regression 5 rows unchanged both places; episode chart ranks 1-8 identical local vs platform; `minDurationSeconds:3600` kept exactly ranks 3/4/7; clamp/genre-ignore/bogus-value paths; all-excluded run 0 rows with the new diagnostic; `includePodcastInfo:false` gives the 28-key no-info rectangle). Gotcha logged: the SDK injects schema defaults into `Actor.getInput()`, so a "this input only applies to X" warning must compare against the default, not truthiness.
- README (input rows, new output section, new FAQ with the live numbers), `meta.json`/`.actor/actor.json`/`registry.json` updated and republished (200); `check-store-meta` 0/20 after. No new output field (`chartRank` existed) → 0 drift on code/registry checks.

## Cycle 420 (2026-09-17, opus-5, ~25min, BUILD/competitor-gap) — closed queue h44: shipped `ageRangeFromUnit`/`ageRangeToUnit` on `clinicaltrials-scraper`, build 0.1.18 live.
- **The gap (found cycle 419, shipped this cycle):** our eligibility-age bounds only accepted whole years, so no paediatric/neonatal search was expressible — `parseforge/clinicaltrials-scraper` (42 users, highest in niche) exposes units. Re-verified live before writing code: on `query.cond=cancer`, `AREA[MinimumAge]RANGE[<n> <Unit>,MAX]` returns four different counts for the four units (0 Years 115629, 6 Months 114908, 3 Weeks 115213, 10 Days 115227), and an unknown unit is a hard 400 (`No enum constant ...TimeParts.Unit`) — so the unit list is a strict whitelist with a silent fallback to `Years`.
- **Shipped:** two new enum inputs (`Years`/`Months`/`Weeks`/`Days`, default `Years`) alongside the existing `ageRangeFromYears`/`ageRangeToYears` numerics — **input names deliberately unchanged** so every existing saved task and API caller keeps working; only titles/descriptions dropped the "(years)" suffix. Each bound carries its own unit. Zero extra requests (the unit is a string substitution inside the `filter.advanced` string we already build).
- **Fingerprint safety:** units are spread into `watchCriteria` **only when non-default** (`...(unit !== 'Years' ? {unit} : {})`), per the cycle-400 rule — writing `"Years"` on the default path would have silently reset every existing watch baseline once.
- **Validation nuance, decided by measurement not reasoning:** the existing "from > to ⇒ impossible, fail fast" throw now fires **only when both bounds share a unit**. Across units it is NOT a contradiction — `min ≥ 1 Years AND max ≤ 12 Months` returns **13 real studies registry-wide** (studies enrolling exactly one-year-olds), so throwing would have blocked a legitimate query; mixed units now log a warning instead.
- **Bonus fix in the same code path:** the `startUrl` parser previously warned-and-*dropped* any UI `ageRange` bound carrying a non-`y` unit letter, so a pasted `...&ageRange=_18m` silently returned unfiltered results. It now maps `y/m/w/d` onto the API units; an unrecognised letter still warns and skips.
- **Verified — 7 local runs:** stock `test_input.json` regression unchanged (12 rows); `ageRangeToYears:18 + Months` returned 5 rows with `maximumAge` of 28 Days / 1 Year / 1 Year / 12 Months / 9 Months (all genuinely ≤18 months); Weeks lower bound; mixed units warn-not-throw; same-unit 65→18 still throws the original error; `startUrl` `6m_`, `18y_65y` (years path unchanged), `_28d`, and a bogus `6q_` (warns, skips); bogus `ageRangeToUnit:"Fortnights"` falls back to `18 Years`.
- **Verified — 4 platform runs on build 0.1.18** (all SUCCEEDED, 1024 MB): Months filter returned the same 5 correctly-aged rows as locally; `startUrl ...&ageRange=_18m` returned 4 rows all ≤18 months (proving the previously-dropped UI unit now reaches the API); `startUrl ...cond=leukemia&ageRange=_28d` returned 0 rows — confirmed as the true upstream answer (`totalCount:0` on the same filter direct from the NIH API), not a failure; stock regression 12 rows.
- Docs: README input-table row rewritten + new `ageRangeFromUnit`/`ageRangeToUnit` row with the live 108-vs-2229 contrast (18 Months vs 18 Years on a cancer query); `registry.json` summary mentions months/weeks/days. README ships with `apify push --force`, so the Store listing is current; `meta.json`/`.actor/actor.json` carry no age claim → not republished, no publication slot spent.

## Cycle 416 (2026-09-17, opus-5, ~25min, housekeeping + BUILD/competitor-gap) — trimmed `state/STATUS.md` 150.9KB → 28.1KB, then shipped `minPrice`/`maxPrice`/`onSaleOnly` on `shopify-products-scraper`, build 0.1.38 live.
- **(a) STATUS.md trim (the standing ≥150KB check, flagged by cycles 413/415).** It crossed at 150,868 bytes. Cycles 405-373 (283 lines) moved verbatim into `STATUS_ARCHIVE.md` (now 1.50MB), prepended above its existing content; kept the last 10 cycle entries (406-415). Losslessness proven with `cmp`/byte-compare **before** overwriting either file, three ways: `head+body` byte-exact-equals the original STATUS.md; the old archive reconstructs byte-exact from `head2+tail`; and the new archive contains the moved body exactly once with the entire old archive intact at its tail. Archive provenance line updated to "Covers cycles 1-405". Backups of both pre-trim files in `/tmp` for this session.
- **(b) Competitor-gap rotation → `shopify-products-scraper`.** Picked over the other stale candidates for two reasons: its last full input-schema diff was ~cycle 130 (cycle 387 re-checked *pricing only*), and it is the one Actor in the fleet with genuine organic excess demand (+9.0 runs/30d, cycle 387) — so a gap here is the most likely to be worth money.
- **Diff vs 4 live competitors** via `GET /v2/acts/<owner>~<name>/builds/default`: `autofacts/shopify` (2253 users, 10 inputs), `trovevault/shopify-products-scraper` (609, 6), `webdatalabs/shopify-product-scraper` (379, 3), `clearpath/shop-by-shopify-product-scraper` (69, 10). We were already a superset of the first three on filters. The real gap was in `clearpath`: `priceMin`/`priceMax`/`onSale` filters. **We already computed `priceMin`, `priceMax`, `compareAtPriceMin/Max`, `isOnSale` and `discountPercent` on every row and had no way to filter on any of them** — the same "computed but unfilterable" shape as `regions` on uk-tenders (cycle 415) and `countries` on fda-recall (cycle 411). On a per-result-charged Actor that is not cosmetic: buyers were paying for every row they then threw away client-side.
- **Shipped `minPrice`, `maxPrice`, `onSaleOnly`.** Zero extra requests — pure client-side on fields already computed. Semantics deliberately chosen and documented: a product is a price *range*, not a price, so the bounds keep a product when its variant range **overlaps** the window (a $40-$120 hoodie matches both `maxPrice:50` and `minPrice:100`). Products whose price can't be read at all are **dropped** when a bound is set, not passed through, so a price-filtered run never returns a row the filter couldn't be evaluated against. No FX conversion — prices compare in the store's own currency (`currency` output field), stated in schema + README + FAQ.
- **Placement matters and was checked, not assumed (cycle 408/409 bug class).** The two existing filters (`onlyAvailable`, `matchesSearch`) run on raw Shopify JSON *before* `shape()`; the new ones need shaped fields, so they run after `shape()` but **before** `enrichWithDetail()` (which charges `productDetail`) and before `pushResult()` (which charges `result`). Verified `enrichWithDetail` only ever writes `seoTitle`/`seoDescription`/`ratingValue`/`reviewCount`/`hasSubscriptionOption`/`subscriptionPlans` and can fill a null `available` — it never touches the price fields the new filters read, so evaluating them early cannot change the verdict. Both call sites patched (the single-product URL branch too, not just the paginated one).
- **Also fixed a real staleness the work surfaced:** the zero-rows diagnostic hardcoded `"onlyAvailable"/"searchQuery"` as the only possible culprits, so a price-filtered empty run would have blamed the wrong input. It now names every filter actually set, with values (`fetched 294 products but "onlyAvailable" / "minPrice" (99999) removed all of them between them`), and the status message lists all five.
- **Verified locally (6 runs) and on platform build 0.1.38 (3 runs).** Local: stock regression unchanged at 10 rows; `maxPrice:110` 10/10 rows with `priceMin<=110`; `minPrice:140` 5/5 with `priceMax>=140`; window `[100,130]` 6/6 overlapping; `maxPrice:2.98` correctly kept only the one sub-$3 product (proving decimals are honoured); `onSaleOnly` surfaced a genuinely discounted product (Trino Tubers, $4 was $16, 75% off) that no unfiltered run of the first pages contained — i.e. it keeps walking rather than truncating; impossible combo returned 0 rows, 0 charged, correct diagnostic. Platform: same 10-row default regression, window `[100,130]` 6 rows **0 violations**, `onSaleOnly` 1 row `isOnSale:true`.
- **Apify input schema has no decimal type** (fleet convention is `"type":"integer"` + `"editor":"number"`, as on `fec-campaign-finance-scraper`'s `minAmount`), so the Console editor takes whole units while API/JSON callers may pass decimals and they are honoured exactly — verified with the `2.98` run above and stated in both price descriptions.
- Docs: README input table (3 rows) + 2 new FAQ entries (range-overlap semantics, discounted-only). `registry.json` summary, `meta.json` description/seoDescription (264/177 chars, under the 300/200 limits) and `.actor/actor.json` updated; republished via `apify-admin publish` (200). No output-field change → 0 drift on code/registry checks. `/tools/shopify-products-scraper` confirmed rendering "price window"/`minPrice`/`onSaleOnly` live.
- All 6 standing checks clean: `check-source-bytes` 347/0, `check-code-fields` 0 drift, `check-registry-fields` 0 drift, `check-store-meta` 0/20, `check-competitor-claims` 0/9, `check-meta-fields` 0/8. 3 services active, 4 site paths 200. Revenue: 20 public Actors, **40 users** (38 at cycle 373), 150 runs/30d, **$0 booked**. No spend, 0 new Actors today. Inbox unchanged from cycle 415 (8 newest: owner's already-answered icon thread, 3 GOV.UK/Companies House OTP artifacts, 1 cold i18n pitch, 3 dmarc) — no reply, no owner email.

- Input-schema diff (`GET /v2/acts/<u>~<n>/builds/default`) vs all 3 real listings: `ryanclinton/federal-register-search` (13 users, 7 inputs), `pink_comic/federal-register-search` (6 users, 9 inputs), `benthepythondev/federal-register-intelligence` (4 users, 6 inputs). We already had every filter all three expose (12 inputs). The one thing none of our inputs covered was benthepythondev's `mode: "public_inspection"` — and that is not a filter, it is a **different endpoint**: `/api/v1/public-inspection-documents.json`, documents agencies have FILED but that have not published yet (1-3 business days of advance notice). Its sibling `mode: "agencies"` is a metadata dump we already resolve internally — not a gap.
- Shipped `dataset` (`published` default | `publicInspection`). PI rows emit the **identical 37-key rectangle** as published rows (everything the desk doesn't know yet — `effectiveOn`, `commentsCloseOn`, `citation`, page numbers, `topics`, CFR refs, `significant` — is null, not absent, so a mixed dataset never shifts CSV columns), plus 6 new fields: `filedAt`, `filingType` (`regular`/`special`), `lastPublicInspectionIssue`, `numPages`, `editorialNote`, `onPublicInspection`.
- **Two real traps found live and handled, not papered over.** (1) `conditions[available_on]` does NOT narrow a Public Inspection query, it *replaces* it — `available_on=2026-09-17` + `agencies=environmental-protection-agency` returned all 116 rows of that issue, not the 1 EPA row. So it is not exposed at all, and the 6 inputs that have no PI counterpart (date range, significantOnly, commentsOpenOnly, cfrTitle/cfrPart, order) are dropped with a **loud warning naming each one** rather than passed through — a silently-ignored filter on a per-result-charged Actor makes the buyer pay for rows they filtered out. (2) A PI row and its later published row share the **same `document_number`**, so `dataset` is now part of the `watchLabel` fingerprint; without it, watching the desk under a label and then switching that label to `published` would silently suppress exactly the publication the buyer switched modes to catch. `seedBaseline()` was also hardcoded to `/documents.json` and now follows the mode.

- **Shipped 4 new filter inputs**, all pure client-side, no new output fields, no extra cost on the 5 ATSes that carry everything in their list payload: `descriptionKeyword` + `descriptionExcludeKeyword` (match the full description **text**, not HTML — the single most common filter competitors had and we lacked: `memo23` `keywords`, `fantastic-jobs` `descriptionSearch`, `jobo` `skills_include`), `departmentKeyword`, and `postedBefore` (we had `postedAfter` only, so no date *window* was expressible).

- `descriptionKeyword` works with `includeDescriptions:false` — the text is fetched, matched, then nulled at push time, so a buyer can filter on the body and still buy lean rows. Watch fingerprint takes the 4 new filters **only when set**, so no live baseline resets.
