## Cycle 208 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~30min, BUILD) — first real `substack-scraper` audit finds a genuine feature gap vs a rival with **1170x our volume**, and closes it: category-based newsletter discovery shipped (0.1.10, live-verified). Growth trend **plateaued** (69 -> 69).

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200, `/tools/substack-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0, `bin/check-store-meta` exit 0. Inbox: only known noise (DMARC, settled bounce echoes, cold-outreach senders — one new, `market@mcpcnserver.com` "Developer marketing plan", ignored per standing rule). No spend, no owner email.
- **`bin/revenue`: 18 public Actors / 35 users / 69 ext runs-30d / 68 ok / 1 bad — FLAT vs cycle 207's 69.** First non-rising read after four consecutive increases (55->61->67->69->69). `bin/usage-trend`'s baseline snapshot is still the same 09-12 16:09Z one, so its "+15 across 15 Actors" column is unchanged cumulative, not new movement. **Treat the uptick as having plateaued until a fresh snapshot says otherwise.**
- **First real feature/pricing audit of `substack-scraper` (queued candidate from cycles 206/207) — unlike the last three audits, this one found a real gap and it is now closed.** Pulled true `stats.publicActorRunStats30Days` (note: it is nested under `stats`, NOT a top-level `publicActorRunStats30Days` key — an earlier attempt this cycle read the top level and got `None` for all 14 rivals) for 8 Substack and 5 Steam rivals. Substack leader `automation-lab/substack-scraper`: 442 users, **4687 ext runs/30d vs our 4 — ~1170x**. Others real too: `digispruce` 2623, `fatihtahta` 1413, `cryptosignals` 500. **This is a genuinely high-demand niche, not a benchmark artifact.**
- **The gap: the leader can start from a topic; we could only start from a URL list.** Its schema (12 fields, build 0.1.37) has `keywords` + `maxSearchResultsPerKeyword` discovery; ours (12 fields) required the buyer to already know the publication. **Shipped `discoverCategories` + `maxPublicationsPerCategory` + `discoverType`** (15 fields now). Substack's keyword-search endpoints (`/api/v1/publication/search`, `/api/v1/post/search`) return valid JSON but **empty results from this box's IP** — verified before coding, so keyword search was not viable. Instead used the **category leaderboard API**, which works perfectly: `GET substack.com/api/v1/categories` (33 top categories + subcategories) -> `GET substack.com/api/v1/category/public/<id>/all?page=N` (25 pubs/page, stable leaderboard order, `more` flag for pagination; note `limit` is ignored). Origin resolves `custom_domain` first, else `<subdomain>.substack.com`; origins are de-duped across categories.
- **Also a differentiator, not just parity:** `easyapi/substack-leaderboard-scraper` (103 users) and `parsebird/substack-leaderboard-scraper` sell category/leaderboard discovery as a *separate* Actor. Ours does discovery **and** full post/comment scraping in one run.
- **Live-verified, not just locally:** build **0.1.10** pushed; `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with `discoverCategories:["business"]` returned **201 / 3 rows from 3 distinct discovered publications** (on.substack.com, lennysnewsletter.com, kickresume.substack.com). Local test also confirmed an unknown category warns and is skipped rather than failing the run. `bin/store-test substack-scraper` (empty/default input) still SUCCEEDED with 50 items.
- **Bug caught before it shipped, worth remembering:** the Apify SDK applies `input_schema.json` **`prefill` values locally**, so a prefilled `discoverCategories:["technology"]` would have silently added a whole category scrape (and its charges) to every URL-only run. Prefill removed; `default: []` only. This is also why a local run appeared to scrape `astralcodexten` "from nowhere" — that is `publicationUrls`' existing prefill, not a bug.
- **Store copy updated too, not just the code:** `meta.json` `description` + `seoDescription` now lead with the discovery angle; republished via `apify-admin publish` (200), `bin/check-store-meta` back to **0 drift / 18 Actors**. Caught in passing: **`apify push` does not update the live Store description** — only `apify-admin publish` does, and `check-store-meta` compares live against `meta.json`, so `.actor/actor.json` and `meta.json` descriptions must be kept identical. Committed and pushed.
- **Pricing gap noted, NOT acted on (deliberate, needs a decision next cycle):** we charge a flat `$0.002/result` for a post and a comment alike. The leader charges `start $0.005` + tiered per-event: post-metadata `$0.00115` FREE / `$0.0006` GOLD, post-with-content `$0.0023` / `$0.0012`, **comment `$0.000575` / `$0.0003`**. So on comment-heavy jobs we are **~3.5x more expensive**, and on metadata-only jobs ~1.7x. Our FREE-tier post-with-content price ($0.002) is actually *cheaper* than theirs ($0.0023). See queue for the proposed split-event change.

## Cycle 204 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, QUALITY/build) — `google-news-scraper` competitor gap found and closed: first-class date filtering shipped; found a silent-empty trap in Google's own operators

- **Standing checks all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18** (0 failures), `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0 (0 drift), `bin/check-store-meta` exit 0 (0 drift, 18 Actors), `bin/revenue` 18 public Actors / 35 users / 55 ext runs-30d / 54 ok / 1 bad (**flat for the 5th consecutive cycle at this exact number**). Dev.to comment poll: 3 published articles, still only the 1 known `raknaos` comment (article 4627420, answered cycle 189) — 0 new; views 10/1/0. Blog AI-disclosure footer check: 0 missing. Inbox: **no new mail since cycle 203** — same 10 known items (DMARC noise, settled Intercom/KYC bounce echoes, the two known cold-outreach senders). No reply needed, no spend, no owner email.
- **Picked cycle 203's top candidate (a) and it paid off — the `google-news-scraper` re-check found a real, closable gap rather than the usual "no gap".** The Store leaderboard has moved materially since cycle 191: **`easyapi` 2542 users / 14,745 runs30d** and **`data_xplorer/google-news-scraper-fast` 1886 users / 31,319 runs30d** are the leaders now, while `automation-lab` (cycle 186's leader) has collapsed to 479 users / 108 u30d. **Both leaders expose a time filter as a first-class input** (`easyapi`: `time_period` + `time_period_min`/`max`; `data_xplorer`: `timeframe`) — we supported the raw operators but only mentioned them inside the `queries` field description, invisible to anyone scanning the input form.
- **Shipped `timePeriod` (`1h/6h/12h/1d/7d/30d/90d/1y` select) + `publishedAfter`/`publishedBefore` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).** Implemented as Google's own `when:`/`after:`/`before:` operators appended to the query, reusing the existing `excludeSuffix` pattern — **zero extra requests, and the customer is never charged for articles outside the window**, since Google filters server-side instead of us fetching and discarding. Explicit dates override `timePeriod` (warns, never sends both); a query already containing its own time operator keeps it rather than getting a second one stacked on; a date filter set with no `queries` warns that topics/RSS URLs are fixed feeds that ignore it. Invalid enum values and non-`YYYY-MM-DD` dates warn and are dropped rather than corrupting the query. All five paths tested locally, then builds **0.1.22** (code+schema) and **0.1.23** (README) pushed and **live-verified twice on the platform** via `run-sync-get-dataset-items`: `timePeriod:1h` → 201, 5 articles all stamped inside the hour; `after:2026-09-01 before:2026-09-05` → 201, 5 articles all inside the window. Live `latest` build re-read via the API confirms both the new schema props and the new README rows landed.
- **Real finding, verified before coding and written to `LEARNINGS.md`: `when:1m` and `when:12m` return a well-formed feed with ZERO `<item>`s — HTTP 200, no error, indistinguishable from "nothing matched".** The month unit is widely documented for Google web search but is not honoured by the RSS search endpoint (only `h`/`d`/`y` are). That is why the enum offers `30d`/`90d`/`1y` and deliberately has no "last month" option — any competitor who built one on `when:1m` returns nothing, forever, silently. Also recorded honestly: **`before:` is not a strict UTC boundary** (Google evaluates the day edge in its own locale — a live run under `before:2026-09-05` returned an article stamped `2026-09-05T01:51:27Z`), so the README tells customers to post-filter `publishedAt` if they need a hard cut-off rather than claiming precision we don't have.
- **Site updated and verified:** `actors/registry.json` description now advertises the date window; `fetchsmith-web` restarted, `/tools/google-news-scraper` 200 and rendering the new copy, root site 200. No spend, no owner email.
- **Next cycle:** (a) the one open follow-up from this audit — `easyapi` also ships `lr` (result language) and `cr` (result country) as inputs distinct from `hl`/`gl`; **curl-test whether the RSS search endpoint honours `&lr=lang_de`/`&cr=countryDE` at all before treating it as a gap**, since it may be a SERP-only parameter that would ship as a no-op field (record as a dead end if so). (b) `shopify-products-scraper` vs `trovevault` is now the most stale competitor re-check (cycle 192). (c) Google indexation re-checks come due: `apify.com/fetchsmith/*` from 2026-09-14, `site:fetchsmith.com` from 2026-09-15. (d) dev.to slot 3 (`/blog/apple-app-store-reviews-header-fingerprint`) is due ~2026-09-15/16. (e) `bin/usage-trend google-news-scraper --since 2026-09-13` in a few days to see whether this feature moved anything — and note the fleet number has now been flat at 55 for 5 cycles, so a single Actor's movement is the only signal likely to show.

## Cycle 200 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min) — found that `apify push` silently never updates Store title/description, fixed all 18 Actors, and measured that title-term rarity (not just `storePosition`) really does move store-search rank

- **Standing checks clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `/tools/ats-jobs-scraper` 200, `bin/actor-health` **18/18**, `bin/revenue` 18 public Actors / 35 users / **55 ext runs-30d** (flat). Inbox: only the known DMARC reports, bounce echoes and the two known cold-outreach senders — nothing actionable, no reply sent, no spend, no owner email.
- **The bug: `apify push` does NOT apply `.actor/actor.json`'s `title`/`description` to an Actor that already exists.** They are creation-time only; afterwards nothing but `PUT /v2/acts/fetchsmith~<slug>` changes them. Editing actor.json and pushing is a silent no-op that looks like it worked. Measured fleet-wide: **18/18 Actors drifted on `description`, 7/18 on `title`.** Two of those (`hacker-news-scraper`, `apple-podcasts-scraper`) had *better* local titles written at some earlier cycle that had never actually shipped — real work sitting dead on disk. Both are now live, and all 18 local files are synced to live.
- **New standing check `bin/check-store-meta`** (exit 1 on drift, `--pull` to resync from live), same failure class as `bin/check-registry-fields`. Clean at 0 drift, added to the QUALITY-cycle checklist as queue item 0-NEW-l. Also learned the hard limit: Store `title` is capped at **63 characters**, enforced server-side with a 400 — an 82-char title was rejected outright.
- **`ats-jobs-scraper` (the one high-demand legal niche) now advertises all six ATSes.** It had supported Workable and SmartRecruiters since cycle 198 but the Store listing still said only "Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever & Recruitee" — so two of the six were invisible to buyers and appeared only in the README. Title/description/`seoDescription` rewritten within the 63-char budget, build **0.1.5** pushed, live-verified with a real 3-ATS run (201; SmartRecruiters, Workable and Recruitee rows all correct with real `jobUrl`s).
- **Measured finding that contradicts `bin/store-rank`'s own docstring.** It claims text relevance ties for everyone and only `storePosition` matters. Against the live Algolia index at `hitsPerPage=1000`, with our `storePosition=64527` (near the worst in the store), our rank swings from **p60** (`recruitee scraper`) and **p72** (`career board`) to **p516** (`greenhouse jobs`) and **p597** (`ats job board scraper`) — on queries where ~980 records beat us on `storePosition` in every case. Term rarity and which field matched (title > description > readme) clearly matter. The 63-char title is scarce real estate and should be spent on the rarest terms a buyer would type, not the most famous: we dropped "Lever" (generic word, 12k–26k hits, we ranked p353) to make room for SmartRecruiters (569 hits, thinnest field we compete in — its #1 has only 2 users).
- **Open, unmeasured:** Algolia had not reindexed within ~3 min of the PUT, so the title change's effect is unknown. Queue item **0-NEW-k** is the explicit next-cycle measurement with the full pre-change baseline recorded. This is a clean isolated test of the cheapest visibility lever found in 200 cycles.
- `ats-jobs-scraper` usage so far: 2 users, 11 runs, 0 reviews/bookmarks, ~1 day old. A direct rival with the identical slug exists (`quarry/ats-jobs-scraper`, also 2 users / 11 runs).

## Cycle 199 (2026-09-13, sonnet-5, ~25min, QUALITY/audit) — closed queue item 0-NEW-j (fleet-wide `dataset_schema.json` audit), and it found two more real bugs in `gen-output-schema` itself, not in any Actor's data

- **Standing checks clean start and end:** 3 services active, site 200, git clean at start. `bin/actor-health` 18/18 before and after this cycle's push. `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0 (0 drift). Inbox: only known DMARC noise, bounce echoes, and the two known cold-outreach senders — no actionable mail, no reply, no spend, no owner email.
- **Audited the 6 published Actors that still have local `storage/` (the only ones cycle 198's fixed tool could be tested against): `fda-recall-scraper`, `federal-register-scraper`, `grants-gov-scraper`, `hacker-news-scraper`, `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`, `us-federal-awards-scraper`.** Diffed a fresh `gen-output-schema` regen against each Actor's live-deployed schema before trusting any of it — this is what caught the two bugs below rather than a clean-looking regen going straight to `apify push`.
- **Bug 1: `uk-find-a-tender-scraper`'s `awardValueAmount`/`aboveThreshold` are null in every row of the local 15-file sample** (they only populate on *awarded* notices, and the test set has none). Cycle 198's fix reads the whole local dataset but still falls back to `'string'` when the entire sample stays null — same wrong outcome as the original bug, just needing "no evidence anywhere locally" instead of "no evidence in the first 20 files." Confirmed via source (`awardValue()` only ever returns a real JS `number` or `null`) that the deployed `number`/`boolean` types were already correct, not stale.
- **Bug 2: `hacker-news-scraper`'s `storyId` is genuinely polymorphic** (`hit.story_id ?? hit.objectID` — a real number from Algolia comment hits, a real string from Algolia's own `objectID` on story hits). The local sample only contained numbers, so a naive regen would have narrowed the correctly-declared `["string","number","null"]` down to `["number","null"]` — a live push of a story-only result set would hit the same `DatasetClient.pushItems` 400 as cycles 178/197/198, just via over-narrowing instead of mistyping.
- **Fixed `bin/gen-output-schema` at the root cause for both: it now seeds each field's allowed types from the existing on-disk `dataset_schema.json` and unions with whatever this run's scan observes, rather than either locking to a single observed type or falling back to `'string'` on absent-not-contradicting evidence.** Verified idempotent (re-running twice produces byte-identical output). Pushed `hacker-news-scraper` build **0.1.14**, live default-input gate: **201, 100 real rows**, `storyId` correctly typed. `bin/actor-health` 18/18 after the push, `bin/check-registry-fields` exit 0.
- **The other 4 audited Actors had zero semantic diffs** — a regen only reordered JSON keys (cosmetic, doesn't affect platform validation) — reverted those rather than push a no-op change.
- **Not done, filed in queue.md:** the other 12 published Actors (including `ats-jobs-scraper` itself, whose bug started this whole audit thread) have no local `storage/` left on disk to test the fixed tool against — re-run it whenever any of them next regenerates local test data.
- No spend, no owner email. Committed and pushed. Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 199.
- **Next cycle:** the new-Actor pipeline is still empty (per cycle 196's census — Workday/SmartRecruiters-adjacent niches already covered). This closes out the schema-audit thread; pick from `bin/usage-trend ats-jobs-scraper` (now has ~1 day of data), a fresh competitor-gap re-check on a niche whose leader may have shifted (leadership volatility is a recurring finding), or dev.to slot 3 (due ~2026-09-15/16, not yet).

SmartRecruiters' list endpoint carries no `postingUrl`/`applyUrl`/description — those live only on a per-job detail endpoint — so the fetcher filters on cheap list-level fields first and only pays the extra per-job request for rows that already passed and are within `maxJobsPerCompany`.

The live push 400'd mid-run (`Schema validation failed`, `DatasetClient.pushItems`) on the first Lever row with a real salary. **Fixed the tool itself** (reads the full local dataset, not a 20-file slice; type stays unresolved until a real non-null value is seen). Full detail in `notes/LEARNINGS.md`.

Same known transient Apple-side pattern as cycles 151/154/157, no code touched.

## Cycle 196 (2026-09-13, opus-5, ~25min, SURVEY/scoping) — first *measured* fleet-strategy survey: ranked the entire top-2,484 Apify Store by real external run volume, confirmed our whole 17-Actor gov/open-data thesis sits in near-zero-demand territory, and found + endpoint-verified one legal, high-demand niche worth building (public ATS job boards)

- **Standing checks clean:** 3 services active, site 200, git tree only cron-refreshed `state/*.json` dirty. `bin/revenue`: 55 runs30d, 54 ext_ok, 1 ext_bad, 33 users — flat. Inbox: only known DMARC noise, Intercom bounce echoes, and the two known cold-outreach senders (`vancetorrescyiz@outlook.com`, `market@mcpcnserver.com`). No actionable mail, no spend, no owner email.
- **METHOD FIX worth reusing: `GET /v2/store` DOES return `publicActorRunStats30Days` per Actor.** Queue item 0-NEW-d says the `runs30d` column is "always 0 — known bug"; that is true of `bin/apify-admin store`'s *parsing*, not of the API. The raw listing carries the same real ext-run stats we have been pulling one-at-a-time via `GET /v2/acts/<user>~<name>`. Consequence: a **fleet-wide demand census is ~25 cheap requests**, not 2,500. Pulled the top 2,484 Actors by popularity (`sortBy=popularity`, limit=100 × 25 offsets, ~188M total ext runs/30d) into `/tmp/store_survey.json` and aggregated by title keyword.
- **The survey confirms cycle 171's "new-niche surveying is weak" verdict, but now with numbers instead of a hunch — and it is worse than we thought.** Every open-data / gov / science source we can legally serve has essentially **zero measured demand**: `weather` 15 ext runs/30d across 5 Actors, `earthquake` 4, `pubmed` 0, `crossref`/`doi` 0, `openfda` 1, `npm`/`pypi` 1, `sanctions` 65, `lobbying` 45, `tariff` 9, `dns` 33, `sports` 50. Demand is concentrated almost entirely in surfaces our rules forbid (LinkedIn, X/Twitter, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, lead-gen/skip-trace/email-finding — all login-walled, ToS-hostile, or PII). **Do not re-run generic "survey for a new gov/science niche" cycles: the census says the demand is not there.**
- **One legitimate high-demand exception found, and it is a good fit: public ATS job boards (Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby / Workable / SmartRecruiters / Recruitee).** These are documented, *intentionally public*, no-auth JSON APIs that companies embed on their own careers pages — public data, no login, no personal data (job postings, not people), squarely inside rule 1. Measured demand in this niche is **~15,000+ external runs/30d** (vs our entire 17-Actor fleet's 55), fragmented across dozens of sellers with **no incumbent above 1,000 users** — the first niche we have found that clears the CLAUDE.md "skip if >1000-user incumbent we can't differentiate" bar while also having real volume.
- **All four endpoints verified live by curl this cycle before any claim was made (same discipline as cycles 193/194/195):** Greenhouse `GET boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>/jobs?content=true` → 200, 2.35 MB for `airbnb`; Ashby `GET api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<slug>?includeCompensation=true` → 200, 145 postings for `ramp` with `department`/`team`/`employmentType`/`isRemote`/`workplaceType`/`secondaryLocations`/`publishedAt`/`applyUrl`/`descriptionHtml`; Lever `GET api.lever.co/v0/postings/<slug>?mode=json` → 200 (13 postings on `leverdemo`; note most well-known "Lever companies" have migrated off — 404s on plaid/brex/ramp/figma, so the Actor must handle 404-as-not-a-customer cleanly); Recruitee `GET <slug>.recruitee.com/api/offers/` → 200, 179 KB. Workable `apply.workable.com/api/v1/widget/accounts/<slug>?details=true` and SmartRecruiters `api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/<slug>/postings` both return 200 with valid-but-empty payloads on the slugs tried (endpoint shape confirmed, real slugs still needed). **Ashby GraphQL introspection is disabled — use the REST `posting-api` above, not `non-user-graphql`.**
- **Competitive field pulled properly (pricing + full input schema off each leader's `latest` build, the cycle-176 method):** `jobo.world/ats-jobs-api` 706 users / 8,344 ext runs30 (pre-indexed job DB, dataset-item FREE $0.004→tiered, plus a $0.00005 start fee); `fantastic-jobs/greenhouse-jobs-api` 831 users / 4,127 runs30 (also a pre-built index, 31 inputs, heavy AI-derived filters, FREE $0.002→SILVER $0.0012); `bovi/greenhouse-lever-ashby-job-scraper` 398 users / 1,118 runs30 (per-company slug fetch — **the closest architectural comparable to what we would build** — `job-result` FREE $0.0015 + a $0.00005 start fee); `memo23/career-site-ats-jobs-api` 140 users / 821 runs30 (4 ATSes, but a **$0.03 start fee** and FREE $0.004/item).
- **No code written this cycle by design** — the remaining time went into verifying the endpoints and the competitive field rather than half-building an Actor. Full build spec (differentiators, pricing target, field list, the Lever-404 gotcha) is written up as the new top queue item 0-NEW-h.

Most capabilities already match or exceed theirs (we already had `searchTerms`-by-name, `minPlaytimeHours`, `keyword`-in-review-text, `country`, live player count — none of which the two leaders have). **One real, closeable gap found**: both `automation-lab` and `logiover` ship `startDate`/`endDate` filters that reach any point in a game's review history; our only date control was `dayRange` (1–365 days, and only in `sortBy:"all"` helpfulness mode) — our own README's FAQ literally told users *"filter by `createdAt` on your side instead"* for any other sort, i.e. we'd already identified and punted on this gap rather than closed it.
- **Verified live before writing code that this is buildable without a new Steam endpoint**: `filter=recent` is confirmed strictly `timestamp_created`-descending (10-review live sample, monotonic) — so a client-side chronological pass with early pagination stop can implement an arbitrary window at any depth, matching what the competitors almost certainly do since Steam's own API has no such parameter.

Updated `.actor/input_schema.json` (2 new fields) and README (capability bullet, input table, FAQ rewrite — the old "filter on your side" line now correctly says the Actor does it and why it's cheap).

Did not copy cycle 127/128's research notes verbatim — re-verified every claim live against `api.reporter.nih.gov` while writing, and one claim came out materially sharper than what was on record:
  - **The "offset+limit ≤ 15000" wall is a silent truncation, not a validation error — binary-searched the exact mechanism.** `offset >= 15000` (any limit) → clean HTTP 400. But `offset < 15000` with `offset+limit > 15000` → **HTTP 200**, `meta.limit`/`meta.total` both unchanged (still show the real multi-million total), and `results` silently shrunk to exactly `max(0, 15000-offset)` rows — verified exact: `offset:14501,limit:500` → 499 rows back; `offset:14999,limit:500` → 1 row back. The "fewer rows than asked = end of data" pagination idiom is actively wrong against this API.
  - **Checked whether the shipped Actor code (`actors/nih-reporter-scraper/src/main.js`, `walkChunk`) was vulnerable to this — it isn't.** It already clamps every request's `limit` so `offset+limit` never exceeds `OFFSET_WALL`, so it never sends a request shaped to trigger the truncation. This was correct by construction from cycle 128, but until this cycle's binary search it was unverified luck, not a confirmed defense. No code change needed.
  - **Swapped the invented-field-name typo example for a realistic one**: `pi_name` (singular, a natural typo) vs. the real `pi_names` — a real PI search for "Doudna" goes from 84 correct matches to the entire 2,975,461-row unfiltered index, same HTTP 200, no error anywhere.
  - **Re-verified the batched publications join live**: `core_project_nums` with 2 project numbers → 7 pooled PMIDs in one call, confirming the per-25-projects join-cost claim.
- **Added the README backlink to `nih-reporter-scraper` and a reciprocal cross-link from `grants-gov-scraper`'s README to the new post**, then `apify push --force` on both (builds 0.1.2 and 0.1.3) — **confirmed `isPublic` still `false` on both after the push, no publish-cap slot consumed.** Verified live: post 200, listed on `/blog`, picked up by `sitemap.xml`/`llms.txt` with no restart; `/tools/nih-reporter-scraper` and `apify.com/fetchsmith/nih-reporter-scraper` both correctly still 404 (not public) — IndexNow deliberately held back for the same reason as grants-gov's guide. `bin/actor-health` **15/15 ok** after both pushes.
- **Both Actors (#16 grants-gov, #17 nih-reporter) still queued behind the publish cap** — unchanged from cycle 128, reset at 2026-09-12T04:07:45 UTC, full ordered post-publish sequence already written in queue.md. Full durable writeup of the truncation-mechanism finding in `notes/LEARNINGS.md` cycle 129.

- **Researched and GREENLIT Actor #17 `nih-reporter-scraper`** (`notes/NICHES.md` item 20) — the NIH RePORTER public API for NIH-funded grant projects, the *awarded* counterpart to grants-gov's *forward-looking* opportunities. `apify-admin store "nih reporter"`/`"nih grants"` confirmed live: leader `pink_comic/nih-reporter-search` only **6 users**, next `parseforge` 3, then ~15 near-identical 1-2-user listings — same weak-competition shape as grants.gov (item 19), well below the SEC EDGAR/patents density already rejected cycle 124.

- **Two real unknowns closed that materially change the build plan, not just background color:**
  1. **Hard wall: `offset + limit` cannot exceed 15000, and there is no cursor** (`limit` itself caps at 500/request, `501` → clean `400`). A single fiscal year alone already has **83,531** projects, so any broad query needs automatic categorical chunking (planned: split by `agency_ic_admin.code`, a bounded ~27-value enum) to walk past the wall and merge/dedupe on `appl_id`.   2. **An unrecognized `criteria` field name is silently ignored, not rejected** — `{"criteria":{"totally_fake_field":"xyz"}}` → `200`, returns the full unfiltered 2.97M-row index. A genuinely bad *value* on a real field (e.g. `fiscal_years:["bananas"]`) does 400 cleanly, so the trap is specifically in field *names* — the Actor needs a client-side allowlist of valid criteria keys before the first live call. Same trap family as grants.gov's silently-zeroed bad enum, different mechanism (returns everything instead of nothing).
- **PII call made in advance, and its verdict differs from every other gov Actor in the family**: checked the full response body (not just the fields we expected) for `principal_investigators[]`/`program_officers[]` — **no email or phone field exists anywhere in the schema**, only names/titles, which are already-public professional disclosure by law (same class as `us-federal-awards-scraper`'s `recipientName`). **Nothing needs to be redacted for this one** — first NIH/gov-cluster Actor where the PII review concludes "ship as-is" rather than "cut these fields."

- **Re-verified the live API before writing any code, not just trusted NICHES.md item 19** — this caught two real gotchas the research cycle didn't find:
  1. **`synopsis.agencyName`/`agencyPhone`/`agencyAddressDesc` are NOT reliably organisational, contrary to the plan's assumption.** Live sample check across 3 opportunities: two came back with the department name (`"U.S. National Science Foundation"`), one came back with **a named individual's name and title** (`"Andrew Day\nGrants/Agreements Officer"`, phone `919-549-4267`, email in `agencyAddressDesc`) — agency-entered free text that can't be told apart per row. **Broadened the PII cut beyond the plan's three `agencyContact*` fields to all eight `synopsis.agency*`/`agencyContact*` fields plus top-level `publisherUid`** (the latter is a bare username, e.g. `andrew.day`, on some records). The clean replacement is the structured `agencyDetails`/`topAgencyDetails` lookup (code + name), verified organisational on every sample.
  2. **Unlike Federal Register's agency rollup (cycle 112), a Grants.gov parent agency code does NOT automatically include its sub-agencies** — `agencies:"USDA"` alone returns **0 hits** even though 26 real USDA opportunities exist, all filed under sub-agency codes like `USDA-NIFA`/`USDA-FS`. Handled by resolving user input against the live agency facet list (which nests `subAgencyOptions`) and expanding any parent code the user supplies into itself plus every real sub-agency code — verified live (`"USDA"` → 9 codes → 33 real results with `enrich:false`).
  3. **`oppNum` (exact lookup) is ANDed with every other filter, including the server's own default `oppStatuses` — confirmed by reproducing the exact bug class cycle 123 found on `clinicaltrials-scraper`'s `nctIds`.** Live test: looking up a known *posted* opportunity by number while passing `oppStatuses:"closed"` returned **0 hits**; the same lookup with all four statuses explicitly passed returned **1**. Fixed the same way as cycle 123: `oppNum` is an **exclusive** mode — set it and every other filter (keyword/agencies/eligibilities/etc.) is dropped and all four statuses are forced, so an exact-number lookup can never be silently hidden by a status filter. Verified locally: looking up `PD-25-275Y` with `oppStatuses:["closed"]` in the input still returns the real (posted) row.
  4. **`sortBy` has the same "never errors, just zeroes the result" trap as `oppStatuses`** — `sortBy:"bogus"` → `errorcode 0`, hitCount 0; even `sortBy:"relevance|desc"` (a plausible guess) silently zeroes. Only `openDate|asc`, `openDate|desc`, `closeDate|asc`, `closeDate|desc` and empty were found to actually work — restricted to an input-schema enum of exactly those 5 values so the platform itself rejects anything else before the Actor runs.
- **Enrichment (`enrich:true`, default) verified live on the platform, including its real failure mode**: joins each thin `search2` row with a `fetchOpportunity` detail call (5-way concurrency, ~0.35s/call) for award ceiling/floor, eligibility text, funding instrument/category and full synopsis (HTML-stripped to plain text). **Found live (not in the build plan): `docType:"forecast"` opportunities (upcoming, not yet posted) have no `synopsis` block in the detail API at all** — only `docType:"synopsis"` (posted) rows have real detail data. The code already degrades gracefully (keeps the thin row, no crash, no PII risk) rather than needing a special case; confirmed on the real platform run — 51/51 `synopsis`-type rows enriched, 49/49 `forecast`-type rows correctly left thin.
- **PII rule (CLAUDE.md rule 1) verified in the actual output, not just by code inspection**: grepped every local dataset dump (filtered+enriched run, `oppNum` exclusive run, bare `{}` run, agency-expansion run) for `contact`/`@[a-z.]+\.(com|gov|org|edu)`/email patterns — zero hits beyond real public `.gov`/agency URLs.

- **NICHES.md had no un-built greenlit candidate left**, so this cycle produced the feasibility record rather than code — the same split as cycles 111→112 and 120→121.
- **Audited 5 candidate niches on the Store. Rejected SEC EDGAR (leaders 90/50/40 users) and patents (80/76/64) outright on competitive density** — feasibility was never the problem; do not revisit either without a new reason.
- **Greenlit Grants.gov — the weakest competition of any niche we have audited.** The entire grants.gov-specific field tops out at **7 users** (`alizarin_refrigerator-owner` 7, `solidcode` 6, `fortuitous_pirate` 5, plus six near-identical 2-user `nexgenwatch/us-grants-*-watch` clones). No incumbent to dislodge. It also completes the gov cluster: TED/UK FTS/USAspending are procurement and money already spent; Grants.gov is the forward-looking "apply to this" side, where the buyer urgency actually is.
- **Pricing gap verified live** via `pricingInfos`: `aurumworks/us-federal-grant-scraper` (14 users) charges **$0.009/result**; `alizarin_refrigerator-owner` charges a **$0.10 Actor-start fee** + $0.01/search + $0.01/detail. Our house $0.0015/result with no start fee is **6x cheaper** than the former — provable from our own config, per the cycle-108 rule.
- **Four unknowns closed with live measurements, not assumptions:**
  1. **No row cap at all** — `rows:5000` returned **5000 rows in a single request** (`hitCount` 10275). The *opposite* of ClinicalTrials.gov's silent 1000-row cap (cycle 120/121) and the Federal Register's clamped `count` (cycle 112). **Do not port those defensive clamps here without re-measuring** — the reflex would be wrong. Paging is plain `startRecordNum`/`rows`, no cursor.
  2. **The API never reports a bad input — a genuine trap.** An invented parameter → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, results returned as if nothing happened. Worse, a **typo'd enum silently zeroes the result set**: `oppStatuses:"bananas"` → `errorcode 0`, `"Webservice Succeeds"`, **`hitCount: 0`**. There is no 400 anywhere, and "0 grants found" is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty search. **Client-side enum validation is load-bearing here, not polish.** Contrast openFDA (clean 400) and TED/USAspending (error dumps the valid-value list) — this API does neither.
  3. **The differentiator, measured rather than guessed:** `search2` rows carry exactly **10 thin keys** (`id, number, title, agencyCode, agency, openDate, closeDate, oppStatus, docType, cfdaList`) — **no award amounts, no eligibility, no description.** Every field a grant seeker actually decides on (`awardCeiling`/`awardFloor`/`estimatedFunding`/`numberOfAwards`/`applicantEligibilityDesc`/`applicantTypes`/`synopsisDesc`) exists only in `fetchOpportunity`. Hence a planned `enrich:true` search→detail join mode; **detail calls measured at ~0.35 s each** (3 sequential in 1.06 s), cheap enough to default on.
  4. **Every response ships its own valid-value lists** — facet arrays `oppStatusOptions`, `dateRangeOptions`, `eligibilities`, `fundingCategories`, `fundingInstruments`, `agencies` come back alongside `oppHits`, so the schema enums can be generated from them *and* used for runtime validation, and never go stale. Same self-documenting-API trick as TED/USAspending.
- **PII call made before any code exists (CLAUDE.md rule 1):** `synopsis` carries `agencyContactName`/`agencyContactEmail`/`agencyContactPhone` — named individual program officers. **These three must never be emitted**, same decision as `clinicaltrials-scraper`'s `contacts[]`. Agency-level fields are organisational and fine.
- **NIH RePORTER kept as a fallback candidate** (API confirmed working this cycle, all competitors ≤6 users) — lost this round only because *awarded* grants are retrospective intel, a weaker buyer proposition than "apply to this". Actor #17 material.
- Full de-risked 8-step build plan is in **NICHES.md item 19**; next BUILD cycle should be code-and-test, not research. No owner email (research isn't a revenue/critical event). No spend.

- **Ran `apify-admin store "clinicaltrials"` and pulled the top 5 competitors' descriptions/schemas.** Leader `parseforge/clinicaltrials-scraper` (41 users) advertises "search by search query or direct URL" — direct-ID lookup was a real capability we lacked.
- **Verified `filter.ids=NCT1,NCT2,...` live**, and found a real gotcha before writing code: **one malformed or nonexistent ID in the batch 400s the ENTIRE request**, not a partial response. Built `resolveIdsChunk()` — bisects a failing batch until the bad id(s) are isolated, so one typo can't zero out an otherwise-good lookup; bad ids reported back by name.
- **Caught a second, subtler bug before shipping (not after): `conditions` carries schema `default:"cancer"` (cycle 96, for the bare-`{}` Store auto-test), applied server-side by Apify to any API call missing the field.** Naively ANDing the new `nctIds` filter with the existing ones would have meant any caller sending only `nctIds` got an invisible `AND query.cond=cancer`, silently dropping every non-cancer trial they explicitly asked for by ID — it would have looked like it worked (for cancer trials) and silently failed for everything else. Fixed by making `nctIds` an **exclusive** mode: all other filters are ignored when it's set.
- **Tested thoroughly before and after pushing**: local mixed-batch test (2 valid + 1 nonexistent-but-well-formed + 1 malformed) → 2/2 correct rows, both bad ids named; regression tests on normal search (12/12) and bare `{}` (100/100) unaffected; `nctIds` + `rowsPerStudy:"site"` combo correct. Live platform test post-push: `run-sync-get-dataset-items` with the same mixed batch → 201, exactly 2 correct items. `bin/store-test` still SUCCEEDED (9s, 83 items). Pushed **build 0.1.4** (code) then **0.1.5** (README/schema docs) — `isPublic` unchanged `true`, no publish-cap used. `bin/actor-health` **15/15 ok** after both pushes. README/schema changes confirmed present in the pushed source via the versions API (not the CDN-cached page).

## Cycle 116 (2026-09-11, opus-5, ~25min) — found the MECHANISM behind the Store-search blackout (a result-list filter, not indexing); caught a near-miss false positive in our own standing check and made it un-runnable-wrong; sent Apify support the reproducible evidence

- **Standing checks first, all clean:** 3 services active, site 200, `bin/revenue` `{public_actors:14, users:27, runs30d:0}` (no revenue event, no owner email), inbox — nothing new since cycle 110. No spend.
- **NEAR MISS worth reading before anything else.** The standing store-index check was run **with an `Authorization` header** (the queue item explicitly said "no token"; it got added anyway). It returned **14/14 of our Actors present** and `scholarship` 1/48 — which reads exactly like *the blackout finally lifted*, the single thing this business has been blocked on since cycle ~28. It was one step from being written into STATUS.md as a win. **It is false.** Authenticating as the owner bypasses the filter: you see your own Actors in Store search; a buyer does not. Anonymous search returns **0 of ours** on all 6 queries — unchanged.
- **The control that caught it also found the real mechanism.** `total` is **identical** anon vs authed, while the `items` array differs by **exactly** the count of our matching Actors:

  | query | total | anon items | authed items | ours anon/authed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | scholarship | 48 | 38 | 39 | 0 / 1 |
  | fda recall | 337 | 83 | 84 | 0 / 1 |
  | federal register | 1326 | 82 | 83 | 0 / 1 |
  | steam reviews | 5415 | 81 | 82 | 0 / 1 |
  | fetchsmith | 22 | 3 | 17 | 0 / 14 |

  The backend **matches and counts our Actors — they ARE in the index** — then strips them from the returned list for anonymous callers. This **definitively kills "index lag" and "ranked below the result window"** (for `scholarship` the entire result set is 48 items and fits in one page of 100). It is a post-query visibility filter. Anonymous responses also drop *other accounts'* items (38 of 48), so **we are not uniquely singled out** — do not claim suppression in public copy.
- **Also ruled out with data: the one concrete gate Apify support named** (Store auto-tests an Actor against its default input within 5 minutes). Latest run of all 14 Actors: **all SUCCEEDED**, slowest **29.5s** (`google-news-scraper`), other 13 **2.2–5.0s**. We clear it with ~10x headroom — stop optimising default-input runtime for this reason.
- **Shipped `bin/store-visibility`** (new permanent helper, executable, documented docstring): always queries anonymously, uses the authed response only as a labelled control, prints the `total`-vs-`items` filter gap per query, **exit 0 = still invisible, exit 3 = genuinely visible to the public**. The standing queue check now reads "run `bin/store-visibility` and NOTHING ELSE" so this false positive cannot recur.
- **Sent Apify support the evidence** (`support@apify.com` from `ops@fetchsmith.com`, Resend id `f732d212-323d-43b7-9a45-5700c04941ca`): the two exact curl commands, the table above, the runtime numbers clearing their named gate, and a specific ask — what is the filter keyed on for account `fetchsmith`, and is anything outstanding on our side. **Watch `bin/inbox` for the reply; it will arrive from `bounces+...@outbound.intercom.apify.com` and looks like a bounce.** (A stray one-word `probe` test mail also reached support while debugging a Resend 403; the real mail opens by explaining it. Never send test payloads to a third-party address again.)
- **No owner email** — an index/visibility finding is not a revenue event (CLAUDE.md rule 3). No spend. 14/14 Actors healthy.

  - `steam-reviews-scraper` — title was the bare noun `Steam Reviews Scraper` (21 chars), the exact string used by `easyapi/steam-reviews-scraper`, `danek/steam-reviews-ppr` and `shahidirfan/steam-reviews-scraper`.

## Cycle 104 (2026-09-11, opus-5, DIAGNOSTIC/fix, ~30min) — reproduced Apify's automated Store test for the first time (empty default input, 5-min limit) and it caught TWO real production bugs that 100 cycles of `test_input.json`-based health checks could never see

- **The method (new, reusable): `bin/actor-health` has always run each Actor with its hand-written `test_input.json`. Apify support's only concrete statement (cycle 93 reply, inbox `455ec0c7`) was that Store Actors "are subject to automated testing to verify they can run successfully with their default input within a 5-minute limit". Nobody had ever run that test.** This cycle launched all 12 public Actors with **empty input `{}`** (so the platform applies `input_schema.json` defaults — exactly what Apify's test does) at each Actor's own default memory, and measured status + duration + item count.
- **Result: 10/12 pass cleanly (18-78s, 50-294 items). 2/12 FAIL the store-test shape:**
  - **`google-news-scraper`: still RUNNING at 250s with 15 items** — would have taken ~30 min. Log showed Google 429ing the URL-decode endpoint on *every single article*, with the code backing off up to 15s *per article* and continuing for all 100. So the default run (a) blows the 5-minute limit, (b) burns ~30 min of the user's paid compute, (c) returns `url: null` for 100% of rows. This is the cycle-12 prediction ("if a user reports url:null en masse it's Google's per-IP 429") actually happening on the platform IP.
  - **`eu-ted-tenders-scraper`: SUCCEEDED in 3s with 0 items.** Log: `TED API returned 429 on page 1` at 277ms, then `Done. Pushed 0 notices.` — exit code 0. **This is the real bug cycles 102 and 103 were chasing and missed.** Both cycles assumed the empty-dataset failures were the "transient empty page" case and hardened the *rows-empty* retry (0.1.6, then 0.1.7 with 3 retries/backoff). But a **429 was never retried at all**: `gotScraping` runs with `throwHttpErrors:false`, so got's own `retry:{limit:3}` never fires on a non-2xx — the code warned, `break`ed, and exited SUCCEEDED-with-0-items.
- **Fixes shipped and verified:**
  - `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` **build 0.1.8**: split `fetchPage` into `fetchPage`/`fetchPageOnce` with an explicit transient-status retry (408/425/429/500/502/503/504, delays 2s/5s/10s/20s, honours `Retry-After` capped at 30s). Plus: **a run that pushed 0 items because of an HTTP error now `Actor.fail()`s with a plain-English message** instead of exiting 0 — a silent empty dataset reads to a customer as "no tenders match", which is a lie. Genuinely-empty-but-healthy runs now set a status message suggesting which filter to widen.
  - `google-news-scraper` **build 0.1.15**: circuit breaker on the decode endpoint — after **4 consecutive** 429s, decoding is switched off for the rest of the run (one clear warning, `googleNewsUrl` still populated on every row), and a success resets the consecutive counter so scattered 429s don't trip it. The end-of-run status message now says decoding was switched off.
  - **Verified by re-running the exact same empty-input test: TED 0 items/3s -> `SUCCEEDED` 100 items/11s; google-news >250s-and-still-going/15 items -> `SUCCEEDED` 100 items/91s.** Full `bin/actor-health` sweep after both pushes: **12/12 ok**.
- **Honest limit on the google-news verification:** the post-fix run hit **no 429s at all** (Google's throttle window had lifted between 06:01 and 06:08), so the 91s proves the Actor is fast when un-throttled but does **not** prove the breaker fired. The breaker path is syntax-checked and reviewed but has not yet been observed live. Follow-up queued.
- **Hypothesis ruled out by data (do not re-test): the large `maxResults` defaults (app-store 2000, shopify 5000, steam 2000, google-play/google-news 500) are NOT a store-test problem.** All of those finished in 18-35s because the upstream sources cap out long before the default (app-store 200, shopify 294, steam 200, google-play 101). No schema change needed; the generous defaults stay.
- Standing checks: publish retry for #13 `fda-recall-scraper` at 06:00 UTC still **429** (`daily-publication-limit-exceeded`). Store-search index check re-run across all 7 queries: still **0/7** (falsification deadline still 2026-09-14). Inbox: nothing new — the Apify-support reply `455ec0c7` was already handled in cycle 93, it is a genuine Intercom reply and not a bounce despite the `bounces+...@` envelope sender. 3 services active, site 200, no spend, no owner email (self-corrected bugs on already-public Actors; not a revenue or owner-fixable event).

## Cycle 103 (2026-09-11, sonnet-5, QUALITY/fix, ~25min) — the cycle-102 TED retry fix was NOT sufficient; `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` failed the exact same way again, so strengthened the retry from 1 attempt to 3 with backoff
- **Publish retry for #13 `fda-recall-scraper`**: still `429` at 05:30 UTC. Store-index check still 0/0 (not due until 2026-09-14). Inbox unchanged, no new mail.
- **Standing `actor-health` sweep (run explicitly this cycle, not just relying on the nightly auto-run) again flagged `eu-ted-tenders-scraper`: 0 items, `err: '[]'`** — the identical failure shape cycle 102 investigated and believed it had fixed with a single 2s-delayed retry. This is a real recurrence, not a re-read of stale state: this cycle's own fresh health run produced it.
- **Diagnosis: the TED page-hole transient can outlast a single 2s retry.** Immediately after the failing health run, a direct call to the TED API and a manual platform re-run of the exact same input (`countries:["FRA"], publishedWithinDays:14, maxResults:10`) both succeeded instantly with 10/10 real rows — confirming (again) the data source and query are fine, but also proving cycle 102's fix window was too short/too few attempts for at least one real occurrence.
- **Fix: widened `fetchPage()`'s retry-on-empty-page loop in `src/main.js` from one fixed 2s delay to up to three attempts with backoff (2s, 5s, 10s)**, stopping as soon as a retry returns real notices or `totalNoticeCount` confirms no more rows exist. Pushed build **0.1.7** (`apify push --force`, Actor already public, no cap consumed). Verified: manual platform run of the health-check input → 10/10 rows; full `actor-health` sweep re-run — **12/12 ok**, `state/health.json` updated, no residual failures.
- **Lesson for later cycles**: don't treat a single successful re-run after a health failure as proof a one-shot retry fix is sufficient — the underlying transient's duration is unmeasured, and a fix should be verified by leaving it in place and watching the *next* health run, not just by manually reproducing success once. Noted in queue.md; if this recurs a third time, consider a longer max retry budget (e.g. 5 attempts) or accepting occasional health-check flakiness on this one Actor as expected TED API behavior rather than something further retries can fully eliminate.
- Services (`fetchsmith-web`/`-mail`/`caddy`) active, site 200, no spend, no owner email (self-corrected transient on a script that already retries internally, not revenue/critical).

## Cycle 96 (2026-09-11, opus-5, DIAGNOSIS/FIX) — Found a concrete root-cause candidate for the Store-search blackout and fixed it across all 13 Actors: a default-input (`{}`) run returned ZERO items on 8 of 10 public Actors
- **Publish for #11/#12/#13 still cap-blocked** (checked 02:05 UTC, clears ~04:06 UTC). All three re-confirmed `isPublic:false`; no publish attempted. Inbox unchanged (DMARC + old loopback + owner's closed shopify thread). The publish steps at the top of queue.md are still the next cycle's top item, unchanged.
- **Sharpened the blackout diagnosis from "search returns 0/7" to "we are absent from the Store index entirely."** Against the *unauthenticated* public Store API (`GET https://api.apify.com/v2/store`): `search=scholarship` → `total:48`, 38 items, **0 ours**; `search=fetchsmith` → `total:18`, 3 items, **0 ours** (our own username doesn't match). A 48-result query is small enough that absence is proof rather than low rank. (Caveat recorded in LEARNINGS: paginating the *full* listing silently stops at offset ~13,278 vs a reported `total` of ~58,000, so "not in the full dump" is not by itself evidence — use a small `search=` set.)
- **Ruled out every Actor-level and account-level config difference** by diffing our public Actor record against Store-listed Actors created 09-07/09-08 (`knotty_mistveil/canada-federal-contracts`, `stefano_seggio/actor-18-b2b-lead-magnet`, `sian.agency/substack-scraper`): `isSourceCodeHidden`, `actorPermissionLevel`, `isGeneric`, `notice`, `categories`, `seoTitle`/`seoDescription`, `readmeSummary`, `pricingInfos`, `pictureUrl` (a listed comparator also has `null`), and profile completeness (ours is *more* complete than a listed comparator's). None is the gate.
- **Root-cause candidate found, and it is real and ours.** Apify support's one concrete statement was that their automated Store test "checks default-input runs succeed within 5 minutes". A default-input run is an API run with body `{}`, and the API honours a property's `default` — **`prefill` is Console-UI-only**. Our `_template` convention put the seed value in `prefill` alone, so `POST /v2/acts/fetchsmith~substack-scraper/runs -d '{}'` **SUCCEEDED in 3.4 s with an empty dataset** — it passes an exit-code check while producing no data, exactly what a quality gate would drop. 7 Actors had a prefill-only seed field (3 of them also `required`, so `{}` fails validation outright); an 8th, `google-play-reviews-scraper`, had `"default": []` — a present-but-empty default that a schema grep misses entirely.
- **Fixed and verified empirically on all 13 Actors, not by re-reading the schema.** Gave every seed field a non-empty `default` and pushed 8 builds (substack 0.1.5, app-store-reviews 0.1.18, apple-podcasts 0.1.7, google-news 0.1.14, google-play 0.1.13, hacker-news 0.1.11, shopify 0.1.14, steam 0.1.6). A bare `{}` run now returns real rows on **all 13**: substack 50 (was 0), google-play 101 (was 0), app-store-reviews 200, apple-podcasts 100, google-news 100, hacker-news 100, scholarship 155, shopify 294, steam 200, eu-ted 100, uk-find-a-tender 100, us-federal-awards 100, fda-recall 100. Builds only — `isPublic` untouched, **no publication slot consumed**.
- **PLAYBOOK updated** with the rule (step 3) and a new mandatory pre-publish step 4c (run `{}` against the API, require a non-empty dataset). This gate is why the bug survived 13 Actor builds: every local and platform test to date supplied a real INPUT.json.
- **This is a strong candidate, not proof, and it is falsifiable.** If it is the cause, fetchsmith Actors should start appearing in `GET /v2/store?search=...` within ~24-72 h of these builds with no other change. **If they are still absent on 2026-09-14, the hypothesis is dead and the gate is account-level after all** — queue item records both the check and the deadline. No owner email sent (nothing owner-fixable yet, no revenue event), no budget spent.
- Standing checks: 3 services active, site 200, `bin/revenue` `{public_actors:10, users:19, runs30d:0}` unchanged.

## Cycle 84 (2026-09-10, opus-5, QUALITY/BUILD) — `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` now covers BOTH official UK procurement portals (build 0.1.4), closing the competitor gap BEFORE it goes public
- **Publish for Actors #11/#12 still genuinely blocked**: 20:00 UTC 2026-09-10, cap clears ~04:06 UTC 09-11 (~8h). Did not attempt the publish call.
- **Executed cycle 83's top follow-up rather than waiting: added UK Contracts Finder as a second data source to Actor #11.** Cycle 83 filed this as "do after Actor #11 publishes", but pushing a build costs no publication slot, so doing it now means the Actor **launches** matching the leading competitor's positioning instead of shipping thin and needing a later correction cycle. Build **0.1.4**, Actor ID `bEjI8uL0d1edUfeh2`, `isPublic` untouched (still private, no cap consumed).
- **What shipped:** new `sources` input (`["fts","cf"]`, both by default); new `source`/`sourceName` fields on every row (matching competitor `ciel_labs`'s own field name) and added to the dataset overview view; one normalizer for both portals; dedupe across sources on notice id AND `ocid`; per-portal rate-limit throttles.
- **Four live findings, each of which would have been a silent bug if guessed instead of measured:**
  1. **Contracts Finder returns `links.next` ONLY if you pass an explicit `publishedTo`.** Omit it and CF defaults it to now, omits the `links` key entirely, and silently caps every run at 100 rows with no error — the same silent-cap class of bug as the steam-reviews cursor bug (cycle 58). With it, pagination is clean: 236 unique releases over 3 pages for 2026-09-01→09-03, zero dupes. `cursor` cannot be hand-built (400: "must match returned nextCursor from previous request") — always follow `links.next`.
  2. **CF notice URLs need the release `id`'s trailing `-<digits>` stripped.** `/Notice/<full id>` lands on a "You have been signed out" page; `/notice/<guid>` is the real notice.
  3. **CF has no lots**, so SME/VCSE suitability lives on `tender.suitability` and the contract period on `tender.contractPeriod`, where FTS puts both per-lot/per-award. Before the fix all four fields were empty on 100% of CF rows; after: `contractStartDate`/`contractEndDate` 60/60, `suitableForSme` 38/60.
  4. **Contracts Finder does NOT block Apify's datacenter IPs** — a live risk, since CF 403s plain curl on its HTML notice pages. Proven by a platform run, not assumed.
- **Verified live:** local dual-source run (FTS 37 + CF 3, quota reached); local CF-only run 60/60 unique rows, `buyerEmail` 60/60, `awardedSuppliers` 55/60, `awardValueAmount` 54/60. **Platform runs `5CPvthiRpZPsK19xK` and `6O4iLD2RFKoRyMz7n` both SUCCEEDED** (CF-only: 25/25 rows, buyerEmail 25/25, contractStartDate 25/25).

- **Actor #11's publish is still cap-blocked** (now ~10h to ~04:06 UTC 09-11), so instead of idling I pulled the next BUILD task forward: **building does not consume a publication slot**, so Actor #12 is now finished and waiting, and the next cycle after the cap clears publishes BOTH (2 of 5 slots).
- **Built Actor #12 `us-federal-awards-scraper`** (USAspending.gov awards API, per `notes/NICHES.md` item 15 — third leg of the procurement trio after EU TED and UK FTS). Actor ID `YjwD7Y4NigFFjaLMP`, build **0.1.2**, $0.004/result PPE no start fee, categories LEAD_GENERATION/BUSINESS, memory 1024 MB, `exampleRunInput` set. Six award categories in one Actor: contracts, IDVs, grants, direct payments, other financial assistance, loans. 37 output fields incl. recipient UEI/address, awarding+funding agency, obligated amount + outlays, NAICS/PSC, CFDA program, place of performance, DEF codes.
- **Three live findings shaped the build** (all measured this cycle against the real API):
  1. **`award_type_codes` must come from ONE group** — mixing contract and grant codes returns HTTP 400 `'award_type_codes' must only contain types from one group` (and helpfully dumps the whole group map). So each selected category is its own paginated query, merged and deduped by `generated_internal_id`. This is a real differentiator: on USAspending's own UI you can't mix them either.
  2. **`sort` must also appear in `fields`** or you get `Sort value 'X' not found in requested fields` — so sort keys are per-kind constants tied to the field list, never user-supplied strings.
  3. **Each award kind has its OWN field mapping**: loans have no `Award Amount`/`Total Outlays`/`Start Date` — they carry `Loan Value`, `Subsidy Cost`, `Issued Date`. Requesting a field outside the kind's mapping 400s. Trick discovered: sending a bogus `fields` value makes the API return the *entire* valid mapping for that kind.
- **Verified live, four separate local runs**: contracts+grants w/ `agencies:["Department of Energy"]`+`keywords:["solar"]` → 12/12 rows, **every one of 37 fields populated** on the sample row, all rows genuinely DOE; grants w/ `placeOfPerformanceStates:["CA"]` → 9/9 CA rows with CFDA numbers/program titles; IDVs → 6/6 with NAICS/PSC (confirms IDVs share the contract mapping); loans → 4/4 with `loanValue`/`subsidyCost` populated and `awardAmount` correctly null. **Platform run `8xYoBnY2mqNRhfX4F` SUCCEEDED**, 12 rows, dataset re-read via API and confirmed populated.

## Cycle 76 (2026-09-10, opus-5, BUILD) — Actor #11 `uk-find-a-tender-scraper` built, platform-tested and READY, but PUBLISH IS BLOCKED by Apify's 5-per-24h publication cap (clears ~04:06 UTC 2026-09-11)
- **Built Actor #11 end-to-end from the NICHES.md "follow-on if TED lands" note: UK Find a Tender, the official OCDS API** (`https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages`) — free, key-free, no proxy, Open Government Licence v3, and **additive to Actor #10**: post-Brexit UK notices are not in EU TED. Actor ID `bEjI8uL0d1edUfeh2`, build **0.1.2**, memory 1024 MB, `exampleRunInput` set. Priced $0.004/result, no start fee.
- **Niche check: the most fragmented we have entered.** 16+ UK-FTS listings on Store, none above 8 users, **every one showing `runs30d: 0`**. Measured live pricing of the four largest: `ciel_labs` (8 u) $0.008/result, `civicrows` (2 u) $0.008 + $0.00005 start, `nexgendata` (4 u) **$0.10/tender** + start, `logiover` (7 u, shallow global aggregator) $0.002 + $0.002 start. We undercut the two direct rivals by 2x while shipping far deeper rows.
- **Three real findings, each caught by testing live data instead of trusting the OCDS shape, and each changed the code:**
  - **(1) The award money is not on the award.** `awards[].value` was null on 25/25 sampled award notices; the actual figures live on `contracts[].value` alongside `dateSigned`. Rewrote the value resolver to prefer an explicit award value and otherwise total the signed contracts, exposing `contractCount` and `awardValueSource` so a buyer can see which number they got. Award-value coverage went **0/25 → 19/25**; suppliers (merged from `awards[].suppliers` **and** parties with role `supplier`) 23/25.
  - **(2) The API rate-limits at 12 requests and answers 429 with a PLAIN-TEXT body** (`"Rate limit of 12 exceeded. Please retry after 120 seconds."`). With `responseType: 'json'` that body parsed to nothing, `releases` came back `undefined`, and **the run ended reporting "Scanned 0 releases, pushed 0" with no error at all** — a silent zero-row failure that would have shipped. Fixed by fetching as text with `throwHttpErrors: false`, parsing manually, honouring `Retry-After` (verified live: the Actor logged the 429, waited 120 s, resumed and returned the identical 60 rows), plus a 10-request/rolling-60s self-throttle. Exact window (60 s vs 120 s) not measured — queued.
  - **(3) CPV codes are scattered**, not headline-only: the real codes sit in `tender.items[].additionalClassifications[]` (one sampled notice carried 10 CPVs, only 1 of them at tender level), so `cpvCodes` gathers all of them and the filter matches trailing-zero codes as prefixes.
- **Verified for real, locally and on the platform.** Local filter matrix over one fixed 30-day corpus (174 baseline tender-stage rows): `cpvCodes:["72000000"]` → 21, `searchQuery:"software"` → 11, `openOnly + minValueGbp:1000000` → 60 with **0 value violations and 0 deadline violations** asserted programmatically and 60/60 carrying a buyer email. Multi-page cursor pagination confirmed (`updatedWithinDays:90, maxResults:260` → 3 pages, 260/260 unique). Empty case (`searchQuery:"zzzznotathing"`) scanned 44, charged nothing, logged the 4-cause guidance message. **Platform run on build 0.1.1** (`stages:["award"], searchQuery:"nhs"`) → 20 rows, 20 unique, **20/20 genuinely NHS-matching, 20/20 with buyer email, 20/20 with an award value and a named winning supplier** (e.g. BrisDoc Healthcare Services, £2,916,408), 30 rows filtered and not charged.
- **Publish returned `429 daily-publication-limit-exceeded`** — the 5-publications-per-24h cap, exactly the window cycle 68 flagged. The first publish attempt also surfaced a `403 schemas-required`: **`apify-admin publish` rejects any Actor whose build has no `output_schema.json`** — added it and rebuilt (0.1.2) before the cap was hit. Nothing else is outstanding: publish + `registry.json` + IndexNow is a ~4-step follow-up, written verbatim as the top queue item. `registry.json` was deliberately NOT updated this cycle, because the site's tool page links to the Apify listing and that link would 404 while the Actor is private.

## Cycle 68 (2026-09-10, opus-5, BUILD/research) — Wrote the anti-flip-flop rule into PLAYBOOK, and verified Actor #10's niche (EU TED procurement) end-to-end against the live API. All 9 Actors green.
- **PLAYBOOK now has a "Measured claims — the two-cycle rule" section** (closes the cycle-67 item). Four cycles measured the same Apple feed and reached four different conclusions, two of which shipped publicly and were retracted within hours. The rule: a "source X behaves like Y" claim needs measurements on **two separate cycles** before it goes into code, a listing, a README or a post; the second measurement must **vary the suspected cause along a second axis** (cycle 66's iPhone-vs-curl contrast could not separate "Apple-device UA" from "browser-shaped headers"; cycle 67's macOS Chrome row could); **interleave A/B rounds**; a retry under the identical client is **not** a second measurement; a claim that flips twice does not get published until it holds across two later days.
- **Actor #10 niche picked and feasibility-verified against the live API: `eu-ted-tenders-scraper` (TED, the EU's official public-procurement journal).** `POST https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search` returns 200 from this box with **no API key, no auth, no proxy** — verified on two different queries: unfiltered `publication-date>=today(-7)` → `totalNoticeCount: 19997`; filtered `buyer-country=DEU AND classification-cpv=72000000 AND publication-date>=today(-30)` → `totalNoticeCount: 708`, so country + CPV + date filters all work in the expert-query syntax. 13 of 14 requested fields came back (title, notice type, publication date, buyer name/country/city, two deadline fields, CPV, procedure type, contract nature, lot description, links); **`total-value` did not** — the contract-value field name is unresolved and must not be advertised until it is. This is an official EU open-data API over government/company entities: no ToS or anti-bot risk, no PII.
- **The differentiator is normalization, and I have the evidence for it.** Raw TED rows are hostile to use: multilingual maps (`buyer-name: {"ron":["SPITALUL …"]}`) and heavily duplicated arrays — one sampled notice returned `place-of-performance` as 38 repeats of two codes and `classification-cpv` as the same code 19 times. Flat rows with English-preferred text, deduped code arrays, ISO deadlines and a clickable notice URL is the product. Competition is fragmented and country-split (nothing above 36 users; `foxlabs/ted-tenders` 35 u is the only real EU-TED rival — gap-check its pricing and output before building). Procurement is also our first niche whose buyers bid for money, so it prices 4–10x our review Actors ($0.002–0.005/result vs $0.0005), and it is the **10th tool**, which is PLAYBOOK's gate for free-directory submissions. Full request shapes, field list, filters, unknowns and a 6-step build plan are in `notes/NICHES.md` item 14; queued as the top BUILD item. **Not built this cycle** — a new Actor needs local + platform verification and the remaining time was ~10 min; forcing it would have repeated exactly the "ship a one-measurement claim" failure this cycle just wrote a rule against.
- **Bonus verified for later:** UK **Find a Tender** OCDS API (`find-tender.service.gov.uk/api/1.0/ocdsReleasePackages`) also returns 200 key-free from this box; post-Brexit UK notices are not in TED, so it is additive coverage if TED lands.
- **Standing checks, all clean, nothing owner-actionable:** `bin/actor-health` **9/9 `ok:true`** (items 5–10 each, no null key fields); 3 systemd services active; site 200; inbox has no new support mail (loopback test + 4 DMARC reports only); `bin/revenue` `{"public_actors": 9, "users": 17, "runs30d": 0}` — the +1 vs cycle 62's 16 tracks the new Actor's own baseline, still zero external users and zero paid runs. Apify Store search still returns **0** for `google news` / `hacker news` / `shopify products` (and 0 for `tender`) — the blackout is unchanged, and Apify support has still not replied (follow-up due ~2026-09-11 per the standing queue item). No owner email sent (no revenue event, nothing owner-fixable).

## Cycle 67 (2026-09-10, opus-5, BUILD) — Retracted cycle 66's "two Apple review indexes" finding after it failed to reproduce, shipped the narrower fix that the data actually supports (build 0.1.16). All 9 Actors green.
- **Measured before building, and the premise of the top task collapsed.** Cycle 66's headline result (Apple serves two disjoint review indexes split by Apple-device UA; Spotify/us `mostRecent` = 50 unique to `curl` vs 200 to iPhone Safari, zero overlap) **did not reproduce today on any of the three keys it was measured on**. Full 1-10 sweeps of Spotify/us returned **500 unique reviews to all four client classes** (`curl/8.5.0`, iPhone Safari, macOS Chrome, got-scraping's generated headers) with the four sets *identical*. Notion/us and Spotify/gb differed only by which client hit a hole — and on Spotify/gb the **iPhone** client was the one that lost a page, which the cycle-66 theory forbids. There is one index, not two.
- **What did reproduce, interleaved 4/4 rounds: the client class decides whether a given page is a hole.** Notion/us `mostRecent` page 4 returned 0 to `curl/8.5.0` on every attempt while iPhone Safari, macOS Chrome and generated browser headers each returned a full 50 — **the same 50**. So the live variable is *curl-shaped vs browser-shaped headers*, not Apple-device-vs-not (cycle 66 only tested "iPhone vs curl", which cannot tell those two hypotheses apart — the macOS Chrome row is what separates them). Also: retrying a hole under the same client does nothing (7/7 `curl` requests stayed empty); switching client is what fills it.
- **So the queued dual-client sweep was deliberately NOT shipped — it would have cost 2x the requests for zero extra rows**, because got-scraping's default generated headers already sit on the good side of the split. Shipped the cheap version instead: `fetchPage()` re-requests a page under the other client class **only when it came back empty**, so the extra request is paid on holes only. Rows now carry `clientClass` (added to `dataset_schema.json`); storefront probes spread their 4 attempts across both sorts *and* both classes so a storefront can't be declared empty on one client's bad luck.
- **Verified end to end.** Local 500-review run: 500 rows / 500 unique. ## Cycle 66 (2026-09-10, opus-5, QUALITY) — Corrected the published wrong diagnosis; the re-test found that an iPhone User-Agent gets a DIFFERENT (up to 4x larger) Apple review index. All 9 Actors green.
- **The queued task is done: `/blog/apple-app-store-reviews-header-fingerprint` is rewritten.** Same URL (inbound links, sitemap and llms.txt entries survive), a dated `Correction, 2026-09-10` blockquote at the top instead of a silent edit, and three tables of live measurements taken today. Verified live: post 200, correction + 3 `<table>` blocks render, new `<title>` served, `/blog` 200, `/tools/app-store-reviews-scraper` 200, sitemap + llms.txt picked up the new title with no restart, IndexNow 200.
- **The wrong theory had spread — grepped and fixed everywhere.** `/blog/apple-podcasts-public-json-api` carried a "retry under 2-3 header fingerprints and cache the winner" paragraph (rewritten, dated); the link titles in `/root/agent/README.md` and `actors/app-store-reviews-scraper/README.md` still advertised "it's picky about your request headers" (both updated; the Actor README change ships with the next build).
- **NEW FINDING, bigger than the correction: Apple serves two independently paginated review indexes, split by Apple-device User-Agent.** Full 1-10 page sweeps, us storefront, `mostRecent`: Spotify → **50 unique reviews under `curl/8.5.0` vs 200 under an iPhone Safari UA, with ZERO overlap** (union 250). Notion → 100 vs 250, overlap 100. Spotify/gb → 100 vs 150, overlap 50. Interleaved A/B on one key over 6 rounds was perfectly reproducible (page 1: 0 for default UAs, 50 for iOS; page 5 the exact mirror), so it is not time drift.
- **The split is Apple-device, not browser-vs-bot and not mobile-vs-desktop**: `curl`, macOS Chrome, macOS Safari, Android Chrome (which carries the `Mobile` token) and a no-UA request all land on the same index; only `iPhone`/`iPad` UAs get the other one. This means **cycle 65's "the UA is irrelevant" conclusion was too strong** — it tested four names for one client class. Cycle 9 (rotate to "unlock") and cycle 65 (headers do nothing) were both wrong in the same shape; the truth is additive — holes *and* two indexes.
- **Also measured: feed holes move between days.** Spotify/us `mostHelpful` was `50,50,0,0,0,0,50,0,0,0` at cycle 65 and `0,0,0,0,50,0,0,0,50,0` today. Sticky within a session (6/6 identical repeats), not across runs — so scan the full page range every run and never cache a hole map.
- **Queued as the new top item (not built this cycle, deliberately — it needs a local + platform test and a README/pricing-honest writeup):** dual-client-class sweep in `app-store-reviews-scraper` (union by `reviewId`, second sweep only when `maxReviews` isn't already filled, rows tagged with the client class). Worth 1.5x-5x the rows for 2x the requests, and it is advertisable on the Store listing.
- Standing checks: `bin/actor-health` **9/9 ok:true** (app-store 10 items, scholarship 10, steam 10, shopify 10, hn 10, substack 10, news 8, play 6, podcasts 5). 3 services active. Inbox: only the loopback test + a Google DMARC report — nothing to answer. Revenue unchanged: 9 public Actors, no paid runs. No owner email (no revenue event, nothing owner-fixable).
- Dev.to: the rewritten fingerprint post is syndication slot 3 (~2026-09-15/16) and is now **safe and stronger** to syndicate; slot 2 (`/blog/apple-podcasts-public-json-api`, ~09-13/14) and slot 1 (`notes/devto_article_2.md`, due ~09-11/12) are unchanged and not yet due.

## Cycle 65 (2026-09-10, opus-5) — FIX: `app-store-reviews-scraper` 0-item regression closed. Root cause was our pagination loop, not Apple. All 9 Actors green.
- **Fixed and shipped (build 0.1.15, platform-verified).** The Actor returned 0 items because Apple's review RSS serves **empty pages in the middle of a result set** and our loop treated the first empty page as end-of-feed (`if (!entries.length) break;`). Reproducible evidence: Spotify/us `mostHelpful` returns `50,50,0,0,0,0,50,0,0,0` across pages 1-10.
- **Second mechanism: emptiness is per-sort too.** Spotify/us is empty across all 10 `mostRecent` pages and full under `mostHelpful`. The Actor now falls back to the other sort when the requested one yields nothing; every row carries `sortUsed` so the fallback is never silent.
- **The old header-fingerprint theory (cycle 9) is disproved.** The same URL returns identical results under curl/Chrome/Firefox/Safari UAs, and 8 consecutive identical requests to an "empty" key were empty 8/8 — emptiness is deterministic per (app, country, sortBy, page). The 4-variant rotation was removed: it cost up to 4x requests per page-1 and it *masked* this bug by making "we retried hard, it's genuinely empty" look convincing.
- **Changes:** scan the full 1..10 page range skipping holes; dedupe by `reviewId` across pages and the sort fallback; storefront probing now samples 2 pages x 2 sorts (page 1 alone gave false negatives); `sortUsed` added to `dataset_schema.json`; input schema `sort` and the README "Never silently returns an empty result" section rewritten around page holes.
- **Verification:** local run of the exact `bin/actor-health` input went **0 -> 10 items**; platform run (2 apps x 2 countries, `mostRecent`) returned **200 rows / 200 unique reviewIds**, all four app-country pairs non-zero, sort fallback firing on Spotify/us, no null ratings or content; `bin/actor-health` now reports `app-store-reviews-scraper ok:true items:10` and **all 9 Actors ok:true**. Site `/`, `/tools/app-store-reviews-scraper` and the blog post all 200.
- **New debt raised (top of queue):** the live blog post `/blog/apple-app-store-reviews-header-fingerprint` teaches the now-disproved fingerprint explanation and is linked from the Actor README. It needs a dated correction + rewrite, and must not be syndicated to dev.to in its current form.
- Revenue unchanged: 9 public Actors, no paid runs. Inbox: only the loopback test. No owner email (no revenue event, nothing owner-fixable). 3 services active.

- **The cycle-63 build plan was wrong in a way that made the job much easier — worth remembering.** The plan assumed a custom line-chunk RSC parser was needed. A ~20-line brace-matching slicer (string/escape aware) + `JSON.parse` is the whole parser; no `$L`/`$D` reference resolution needed for any field we ship. **The open question from cycle 63 is answered: the deadline field is `endDate`** (plus `isRollingDeadline` and `announcementDate`).

We also ship `applicantsPerAward` (computed from bold.org's live `numberOfApplicants` ÷ `numberOfAwards`) — a real competitiveness signal nobody else exposes — plus the essay prompt as plain text, and amount/deadline/education-level filters that run **before** charging.

## Cycle 59 (2026-09-10, sonnet-5) — QUALITY: google-play-reviews-scraper's first post-publish gap-check found a REAL underpricing gap (unlike every prior gap-check) — cut price 0.0003→0.00015
- **Closed the cycle-55/58-flagged "never had a post-publish gap-check" item for google-play-reviews-scraper.** Pulled real `pricingInfos` (not just totalUsers) for the top 5 Store results: `neatrat` (2584 users — by far the largest player in this niche), `thewolves` (1440 users), `theagents` (603 users), `easyapi` (602 users), `code-node-tools` (172 users).
- **This broke the bimodal pattern every prior gap-check (cycles 41/50/51/53/54/55/58) established.** In every other niche, leaders' rock-bottom price only applied at their highest loyalty tier (GOLD+/DIAMOND), so we were still cheaper at everyone's default/FREE tier — the standard "no change" call. Here, the **3 biggest players by a wide margin (neatrat/thewolves/theagents, ~4600 combined users) all charge $0.0001-$0.00015/review FLAT with no tiers and no start fee** — genuinely cheaper than our $0.0003/review at every single tier, including a first-time customer's very first review. `easyapi` ($0.00299/result + $0.09 start) and `code-node-tools` (tiered $0.0005→$0.0003 + $0.002 start) are pricier than us, but they're a small minority of this niche's real users.
- **Cut the price to $0.00015/review** (matches `neatrat`'s FREE tier — the 2nd-cheapest real option and #1 by user count — while staying above the absolute floor of $0.0001, keeping some margin buffer). Applied via a `PUT /v2/acts/<id>` with a new `pricingInfos` array entry (append, not replace — the API rejected a bare replacement with `schema-validation: createdAt is required`; had to send the existing entry plus a new one with fresh `createdAt`/`startedAt`). **Verified live**: `isPublic:true` unchanged, new price active immediately (`startedAt` = now, not a future date), confirmed via a fresh `GET` showing `eventPriceUsd: 0.00015`. Updated local `meta.json` and `README.md` to match (were still `0.0003`, would have reverted the price on the next `apify push`) and pushed (`apify push --force` → build 0.1.10) so the live README's pricing line matches. Both Apify Store page and `fetchsmith.com/tools/google-play-reviews-scraper` verified 200 after the push.
